The Darboux coordinates (ξΛ, ξ̃Λ, α) on ℤ are piecewise holomorphic functions satisfying the contact Hamiltonian equations ∂tξΛ = {ξΛ, H}, where H is the contact Hamiltonian generating the real structure. For examiners, the core facts are: (1) the c-map twistor space is a contact manifold fibred over ℙ¹ with real structure; (2) the Seiberg–Witten curve provides the spectral data for the rigid special Kähler base; (3) instanton corrections appear as wall-crossing of Darboux coordinates on ℤ; (4) the contact Hamiltonian generates the real structure and encodes the quaternionic Kähler metric; (5) the twistor construction solves the problem of finding the exact hypermultiplet metric including all quantum corrections.

Worked Problem: Contact Hamiltonian for the Universal Hypermultiplet
The universal hypermultiplet in type IIA string theory on a Calabi–Yau threefold has a classical quaternionic Kähler metric on ℳH = SU(2,1)/SU(2)×U(1). The twistor space ℤ is the flag manifold F(1,2;3) = SU(2,1)/U(1)×U(1) fibred over ℙ¹. The Darboux coordinates are ξ⁰ = 1, ξ¹ = ζ, ξ̃₀ = -i(σ + ½ζζ̄), ξ̃₁ = iζ̄, α = log(ζ̄/ζ) + iφ, where ζ is the coordinate on the ℙ¹ fibre, σ is the dilaton, and φ is the axion. The contact one-form is τ = dα + ξ̃Λ dξΛ - ξΛ dξ̃Λ. Compute the contact Hamiltonian H generating the real structure ζ ↦ -1/ζ̄, and verify that the quaternionic Kähler metric is recovered from the twistor data.
The real structure acts as ζ ↦ -1/ζ̄, σ ↦ σ + log|ζ|², φ ↦ -φ. The contact Hamiltonian H is defined by ιVτ = H, where V is the vector field generating the real structure. On the twistor space, V = i(ζ∂ζ - ζ̄∂ζ̄) + i(∂φ - ∂φ̄) + ... The contact form in Darboux coordinates is τ = dα + ξ̃₀ dξ⁰ + ξ̃₁ dξ¹ - ξ⁰ dξ̃₀ - ξ¹ dξ̃₁. Substituting the Darboux coordinates: τ = dα - i(σ + ½ζζ̄)d(1) + iζ̄ dζ - 1·d(-i(σ + ½ζζ̄)) - ζ·d(iζ̄) = dα + iζ̄ dζ + i dσ + ½i(ζ̄ dζ + ζ dζ̄) - iζ dζ̄ = dα + i dσ + ½i(ζ̄ dζ - ζ dζ̄). The vector field V = i(ζ∂ζ - ζ̄∂ζ̄) + ∂φ (since α = log(ζ̄/ζ) + iφ, the real structure flips φ). Then ιVτ = i(ζ∂ζ - ζ̄∂ζ̄)⌟[½i(ζ̄ dζ - ζ dζ̄)] + ∂φ⌟dα = ½i(ζζ̄ + ζ̄ζ) + i = i(ζζ̄ + 1). Thus H = i(1 + |ζ|²). The quaternionic Kähler metric is recovered from the twistor data via the Legendre transform of the contact potential Φ = log(1 + |ζ|²) + σ, yielding the SU(2,1)/SU(2)×U(1) metric ds² = dσ² + e²σ(dφ + ½i(ζ̄ dζ - ζ dζ̄))² + eσ|dζ|²/(1+|ζ|²)², which matches the known universal hypermultiplet metric.

Twistor Methods for Quantum Field Theory on Curved Spacetimes and the Unruh Effect

Twistor theory provides a non-local description of quantum fields on curved spacetimes that makes conformal symmetry manifest. For a massless field of helicity h on a conformally flat spacetime, the twistor Penrose transform maps the field to a cohomology class in H¹(ℙ𝒯, 𝒪(2h-2)), where ℙ𝒯 is the projective twistor space of the conformal compactification. On a general curved spacetime, the twistor space is not a complex manifold but a CR manifold, and the Penrose transform is replaced by the twistor cohomology of the sheaf of solutions to the twistor equation ∇A'(AωB) = 0. The Unruh effect — the thermal spectrum seen by an accelerated observer in Minkowski space — has a clean twistor description. The Rindler wedge is the region x² > t², and its boundary is the null plane ℐ⁺ ∩ ℐ⁻. The twistor space of the Rindler wedge is the subset of ℙ𝒯 where the incidence relation μA' = ixAA'λA yields points with x² > t². This subset is a tube domain in ℙ𝒯, and the accelerated observer's vacuum corresponds to a specific choice of positive-frequency modes on this tube domain. The Bogoliubov transformation between Minkowski and Rindler modes is implemented by a conformal transformation on ℙ𝒯 that maps the tube domain to the standard upper half-plane. The thermal factor e-2πω/a arises from the periodicity of the conformal factor under the boost Killing vector, which acts on twistor space as a rotation of the ℙ¹ fibres. For a black hole spacetime, the twistor space has a similar tube domain structure near the horizon, and the Hawking temperature is again encoded in the periodicity of the conformal factor. The twistor approach also clarifies the origin of the entanglement entropy: the reduced density matrix for the Rindler wedge is obtained by tracing over the complementary wedge, which in twistor space corresponds to restricting the cohomology class to the tube domain and taking the modulus squared. The replica trick for computing entanglement entropy becomes a computation of the partition function on an n-sheeted cover of the twistor tube domain. For examiners, the essential points are: (1) the twistor space of a Rindler wedge is a tube domain in ℙ𝒯; (2) the Unruh temperature arises from the periodicity of the conformal factor under the boost action on twistor space; (3) the Bogoliubov transformation is a conformal map on ℙ𝒯; (4) entanglement entropy is computed by restriction of twistor cohomology to the tube domain; (5) the method extends to black hole horizons via the near-horizon twistor geometry.

Twistor Description of Integrable Defects and Boundary Conditions in 2D QFT

Integrable defects in two-dimensional quantum field theories are codimension-one interfaces that preserve integrability. The twistor description of such defects uses the fact that the classical integrable field equations (sine-Gordon, affine Toda, principal chiral model) arise as symmetry reductions of the self-dual Yang–Mills equations on ℝ²,². A defect is a discontinuity in the field configuration along a line, and the condition that the defect preserves integrability is that the monodromy of the Lax connection across the defect is a gauge transformation. In twistor space, the Lax connection is the pullback of the holomorphic connection on the twistor bundle ℤ → ℙ¹, and the defect corresponds to a jump in the trivialisation of the bundle across a divisor D ⊂ ℤ. The defect conditions are encoded in a meromorphic gauge transformation g(z) on ℤ with poles along D, satisfying a factorisation condition g(z) = g+(z)g-(z)⁻¹ where g± are holomorphic on either side of D. This is a Riemann–Hilbert problem on ℤ with a prescribed jump across D. The space of defect conditions is then the space of solutions to this Riemann–Hilbert problem, which is a Poisson–Lie group. For the sine-Gordon model, the defect is a Bäcklund transformation, and the twistor description yields the classical r-matrix structure: the defect matrix K(λ) satisfies the reflection equation K₁(λ)r(λ/μ)K₂(μ)r(λμ) = r(λμ)K₂(μ)r(λ/μ)K₁(λ), where r is the classical r-matrix of the affine Lie algebra. Boundary conditions are a special case where the defect is placed at the boundary of the half-line. The twistor space for the half-line is the quotient of ℤ by the involution corresponding to the boundary, and the boundary condition is a Lagrangian submanifold in the symplectic leaf of the Poisson–Lie group. The quantum reflection matrix is obtained by quantising the classical r-matrix, and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation emerges from the associativity of the operator product expansion of defect operators in the twistor string. For examiners, the core facts are: (1) integrable defects correspond to meromorphic gauge transformations on twistor space with prescribed jumps; (2) the defect matrix satisfies the classical reflection equation; (3) boundary conditions are Lagrangian submanifolds in the Poisson–Lie group of defect matrices; (4) the quantum reflection matrix satisfies the boundary Yang–Baxter equation; (5) the twistor string computes defect correlation functions via open string amplitudes on the worldsheet with boundary conditions on D-branes wrapping the defect divisor.

Twistor Theory and the Geometry of Scattering Forms: From Amplituhedron to Associahedron

The scattering form is a differential form on the kinematic space whose residues at physical poles give the scattering amplitudes. In planar N = 4 SYM, the tree-level scattering form is the canonical form of the amplituhedron An,k ⊂ G(k, k+4), a positive geometry defined by the positivity of all ordered minors of the momentum twistor matrix Z ∈ G+(k, n). The canonical form Ω = ∑vertices ∏edges d log Xe has logarithmic singularities on the boundaries of the amplituhedron, which correspond to physical factorisation channels. The amplituhedron is a projection of the positive Grassmannian G+(k, n) via the map Z ↦ Y = C·Z, where C ∈ G+(k, n). The boundaries of the amplituhedron are in bijection with the cells of G+(k, n), and the triangulation of the amplituhedron corresponds to a choice of BCFW recursion. For non-planar amplitudes and for theories with less supersymmetry, the amplituhedron is replaced by other positive geometries. The associahedron is the positive geometry for bi-adjoint φ³ theory: its canonical form gives the tree-level scattering amplitudes of massless scalars with cubic interactions. The associahedron is a polytope whose vertices correspond to planar binary trees, and its facets correspond to factorisation channels where a subset of momenta goes on-shell. The kinematic space for φ³ theory is the space of Mandelstam variables sij = (pi + pj)², and the associahedron is defined by the linear inequalities sI ≥ 0 for all subsets I of external legs, together with the momentum conservation constraints. The twistor description of the associahedron uses the fact that the Mandelstam variables are brackets of momentum twistors: sij = ⟨i j i+1 j+1⟩. The positive geometry is then the region in momentum twistor space where all planar brackets are positive, which is precisely the positive Grassmannian G+(2, n) for the bi-adjoint scalar. For general effective field theories, the positive geometry is the EFT-hedron, defined by positivity of the coefficients in the low-energy expansion of the scattering amplitude. The EFT-hedron is a projection of the amplituhedron by a map that implements the soft limit, and its canonical form reproduces the positivity bounds on Wilson coefficients. For examiners, the essential points are: (1) the scattering form is the canonical form of a positive geometry in kinematic space; (2) the amplituhedron is the positive geometry for planar N = 4 SYM; (3) the associahedron is the positive geometry for bi-adjoint φ³ theory; (4) the EFT-hedron encodes positivity bounds for general effective field theories; (5) all these geometries are regions in momentum twistor space defined by positivity of planar brackets.

Twistor Theory and the Cosmological Bootstrap: Wavefunction of the Universe in Twistor Space

The cosmological bootstrap programme reconstructs the wavefunction of the universe Ψ[φ] from symmetry principles — de Sitter isometries, unitarity, locality, and analyticity — without invoking a bulk time evolution. The Twistor Description of Cluster Algebras and Symbol Alphabets in Scattering Amplitudes

Scattering amplitudes in planar N = 4 SYM are polylogarithmic functions whose symbol alphabets — the set of logarithmic differentials d log φi appearing in the symbol — are governed by cluster algebras associated to the Grassmannian G(k,n). The cluster variables φi are Plücker coordinates ⟨i1…ik⟩ on G(k,n), and the cluster mutations correspond to the tropicalisation of the Plücker relations. In momentum twistor space, the kinematic variables are the four-brackets ⟨i j k l⟩ = εABCD ZiA ZjB ZkC ZlD, and the symbol alphabet for n-particle MHV amplitudes is the set of all four-brackets together with the six-brackets ⟨i j k l m n⟩ that appear at two loops and beyond. The cluster algebra structure is the coordinate ring of the affine cone over the Grassmannian G(4,n), and the cluster variables are in bijection with the diagonals of an n-gon (for k=2) or with the T-system/Y-system of the integrable spin chain (for general k). The symbol of the n-particle MHV amplitude at L loops is a sum of tensor products of d log of cluster variables, with coefficients determined by the positive geometry of the amplituhedron. For example, the two-loop MHV amplitude for n=6 has symbol alphabet of 9 letters: the 6 four-brackets ⟨i i+1 i+2 i+3⟩ and the 3 six-brackets ⟨1 2 3 4 5 6⟩, ⟨1 3 5 2 4 6⟩, ⟨1 4 2 5 3 6⟩. The cluster mutation sequence corresponds to the BCFW recursion in twistor space: each BCFW shift Zn → Zn + z Z1 induces a mutation on the cluster algebra, and the recursion terminates when the cluster variable reaches a frozen variable (a four-bracket of adjacent particles). The symbol alphabet for non-MHV amplitudes involves the cluster algebra of the Grassmannian G(k,n) with k>2, and the letters are the Plücker coordinates ⟨i1…ik⟩. The coproduct structure of the amplitude — the decomposition into lower-loop and lower-point pieces — is encoded in the cluster algebra's comultiplication, which is dual to the mutation. For examiners, the essential facts are: (1) the symbol alphabet of planar N = 4 SYM amplitudes is the set of cluster variables of the Grassmannian cluster algebra; (2) cluster mutations correspond to BCFW shifts in momentum twistor space; (3) the amplituhedron's boundary stratification is the cluster complex; (4) the coproduct of the amplitude matches the cluster algebra comultiplication; (5) the symbol alphabet for n=6 MHV at two loops has 9 letters, for n=7 MHV at two loops has 42 letters, and the number grows as the number of cluster variables in the corresponding cluster algebra.

Exam Strategy: Cluster Algebras in Amplitudes
When asked about symbol alphabets, always identify the Grassmannian G(k,n) first. For MHV, k=2 and the alphabet is four-brackets; for NMHV, k=3 and the alphabet includes three-brackets. The number of cluster variables for G(k,n) is k(n−k) + 1 for the coefficient-free case; with coefficients it is larger. The exchange matrix B is the signed adjacency matrix of the quiver whose nodes are the cluster variables. BCFW recursion = cluster mutation sequence. This mapping is a favourite examiner shortcut: if you see a BCFW shift, think cluster mutation.

Twistor Geometry of Solvable Irrelevant Deformations: TTbar and JTbar in Twistor Space

The TTbar deformation of a two-dimensional quantum field theory is defined by the flow equation ∂λ Sλ = ∫ d2x det Tμν, where Tμν is the stress tensor. In twistor space, the deformation has a geometric interpretation as a modification of the twistor correspondence for the worldsheet theory. The undeformed CFT2 corresponds to a holomorphic vector bundle E → ℙ1 with a flat connection ∂̅E. The TTbar deformation introduces a non-commutative deformation of the twistor space: the incidence relation xαα̇ = λα ̃λα̇ is replaced by a star-product xαα̇ ⋆ = λα ̃λα̇ + iλ θαβ ∂β ̃λα̇ + …, where θαβ is the deformation parameter. The deformed stress tensor Tμν(λ) is the Noether current of the deformed translation symmetry, and its determinant det Tμν becomes the Jacobian of the map from the deformed twistor space to the deformed spacetime. The flow equation ∂λ S = ∫ det T is then the statement that the deformed action is the generating function for the symplectomorphism of the twistor phase space induced by the deformation. For the JTbar deformation (where J is a U(1) current), the twistor description involves a deformation of the contact structure on the twistor space ℙ3|4 of N = 4 SYM. The current J corresponds to a holomorphic vector field V on ℙ3|4 preserving the contact form η, and the deformation parameter λ couples to the Lie derivative ℒV η. The deformed theory is described by a new contact structure ηλ = η + λ ℒV η + O(λ2), and the partition function on a Riemann surface Σ is computed by the holomorphic anomaly equation in the deformed twistor space. The energy spectrum of the deformed theory on a cylinder of circumference R is given by the CDD formula En(R,λ) = (R/2λ)(1 − √(1 − 4λEn(R,0)/R2 + 4λPn/R)), which in twistor space arises from the quantisation of the deformed symplectic form ωλ = ω + λ d(ιV η) on the twistor phase space. For examiners, the key points are: (1) TTbar deformation = non-commutative deformation of the twistor incidence relation; (2) the flow equation is the generating function for a symplectomorphism of twistor phase space; (3) JTbar deformation = deformation of the contact structure on supertwistor space; (4) the CDD energy formula follows from quantisation of the deformed symplectic form; (5) the deformed S-matrix is the CDD factor Sλ(s) = exp(iλ s/2) S0(s), which in twistor space is the phase shift from the deformed incidence relation.

The Twistor Correspondence for the Quantum Spectral Curve in AdS5/CFT4

The quantum spectral curve (QSC) is the exact solution of the spectral problem for planar N = 4 SYM on ℝ × S3 (or equivalently, type IIB string theory on AdS5 × S5). It is a system of Riemann-Hilbert equations for a set of Q-functions Qa(u), Qa|i(u), Qa|i|j(u), … defined on the spectral parameter plane u ∈ ℂ, with branch cuts and asymptotics determined by the quantum numbers of the state. In twistor space, the QSC arises from the monodromy of the Lax connection of the classical string sigma model on AdS5 × S5, which is a flat connection on the twistor space ℙ3|4 × ℙ3|4 of the supercoset PSU(2,2|4)/SO(4,1) × SO(5). The spectral parameter u is the coordinate on the ℙ1 fibre of the twistor space, and the Q-functions are the components of the fundamental solution of the Lax equation ∂u Ψ = L(u) Ψ, where L(u) is the Lax matrix valued in the Lie superalgebra psu(2,2|4). The Riemann-Hilbert equations of the QSC are the analyticity and gluing conditions for Ψ(u) across the branch cuts, which correspond to the positions of the Bethe roots in the thermodynamic limit. The Pμ-system of the QSC — the relation between the P-functions (polynomials in u) and the μ-functions (periodic functions of u) — is the twistor space incarnation of the Plücker relations for the Grassmannian G(4|4, 4|4) of the supercoset. The exact spectrum of anomalous dimensions γ(g) for any operator is obtained by solving the QSC, which in twistor language means finding the monodromy data of the flat connection on the twistor space that satisfies the required analyticity and asymptotic conditions. For the Konishi operator at four loops, the QSC reproduces γ = 12g2 − 48g4 + 336g6 − (2820 + 288ζ3)g8 + …, where g2 = λ/(16π2). The twistor derivation of this result uses the fact that the Lax connection is the pullback of the Maurer-Cartan form on the supercoset to the worldsheet, and the spectral parameter u is the twistor coordinate on the ℙ1 of the Lax pair. The quantum corrections to the classical spectral curve come from the worldsheet instantons, which in twistor space are holomorphic curves in ℙ3|4 × ℙ3|4 with boundary on the D-brane wrapping the defect. For examiners, the essential facts are: (1) the QSC is the monodromy problem for the Lax connection on the twistor space of AdS5 × S5; (2) the spectral parameter u is the twistor coordinate on the ℙ1 fibre; (3) the Pμ-system is the Plücker relations for the super-Grassmannian; (4) the exact anomalous dimensions are obtained by solving the Riemann-Hilbert problem on the twistor space; (5) the Konishi anomalous dimension at four loops is a standard benchmark that must be reproducible from the QSC.

Twistor Methods for the S-Matrix Bootstrap: Unitarity and Crossing in Twistor Space

The S-matrix bootstrap programme aims to constrain and compute scattering amplitudes using only the fundamental principles of unitarity, crossing symmetry, analyticity, and polynomial boundedness, without reference to a Lagrangian. In twistor space, these principles acquire a geometric formulation. Unitarity of the S-matrix, S†S = 1, translates into the statement that the twistor space amplitude A(Z1,…,Zn) satisfies a cutting rule: the discontinuity across a physical pole is the product of lower-point amplitudes integrated over the on-shell phase space. In momentum twistor space, the phase space integral becomes a contour integral over the positive Grassmannian G+(k,n), and the cutting rule is the statement that the canonical form of the amplituhedron factorises on its boundaries. Crossing symmetry — the analytic continuation of the amplitude from the s-channel to the t-channel — corresponds to the cluster mutation in the Grassmannian cluster algebra that exchanges the frozen variables associated with the two channels. The Mandelstam variables sij = ⟨i j i+1 j+1⟩ are the cluster variables, and crossing is the mutation that changes the triangulation of the amplituhedron. Polynomial boundedness (the Froissart-Martin bound) translates into the condition that the twistor amplitude has at most polynomial growth in the kinematic invariants, which in the positive geometry language means the canonical form has logarithmic singularities only on the boundaries of the amplituhedron, not in the interior. The dispersion relations for the amplitude — the integral representations that express the amplitude in terms of its discontinuities — become the BCFW recursion relations in twistor space, which are the statement that the canonical form of the amplituhedron can be triangulated by a sequence of BCFW shifts. For the 2 → 2 scattering of identical scalars in a theory with a mass gap, the S-matrix bootstrap in twistor space reduces to the problem of finding a function A(s,t) analytic in the cut s-plane and t-plane, crossing symmetric A(s,t) = A(t,s), unitary Im A(s,0) ≥ |A(s,0)|2, and bounded by s2. The twistor space of this problem is the space of four momentum twistors Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4 modulo GL(2), and the amplitude is a function of the single cross-ratio u = ⟨1234⟩2/⟨1234⟩⟨3412⟩. The bootstrap equations become a set of integral equations for the discontinuity of A(u) across the cuts u ∈ [0,1] and u ∈ [1,∞). For examiners, the key points are: (1) unitarity = factorisation of the amplituhedron canonical form on boundaries; (2) crossing = cluster mutation in the Grassmannian cluster algebra; (3) polynomial boundedness = logarithmic singularities only on boundaries; (4) dispersion relations = BCFW recursion = triangulation of the amplituhedron; (5) the 2 → 2 bootstrap in twistor space is a single-variable problem for the cross-ratio u.

Twistor Geometry of the Light-Front Hamiltonian and Null-Plane Quantization

The light-front formulation of quantum field theory chooses a null plane x⁺ = 0 as the quantisation surface. In twistor language the null plane corresponds to a projective line in twistor space that is fixed by a real structure τ of split signature. The incidence relation Z^α = (ω^A, πA′) with ω^A = i xAA′ πA′ reduces on the null plane to ω^A = i x⁻ π^A, so the twistor coordinates split into dynamical πA′ and constrained ω^A. The light-front Hamiltonian becomes the generator of translations in x⁺ and is represented on twistor space by the operator H = ∫ d²π π̄ π 𝒪(π,π̄) where 𝒪 is the twistor field of helicity h. This representation makes the kinematic Poincaré generators linear in the twistor variables, while the dynamical generators acquire the non‑local interaction kernels familiar from the MHV Lagrangian.

A key advantage is that the light-front vacuum is trivial: all particles have positive light-front momentum p⁺ > 0, so the Fock space builds directly on the empty state. In twistor space this translates into the statement that the cohomology group H¹(ℙ¹, 𝒪(−2h−2)) vanishes for the physical helicities, eliminating zero‑mode contributions. The Hamiltonian evolution is then generated by a contour integral over the Riemann sphere of the twistor action S = ∫ d⁴x d⁸θ ℒ(Φ) pulled back to the null plane, which yields the familiar light‑front Hamiltonian density ℋ = Tr(∂⁻Φ ∂⁻Φ) + g Tr(Φ ∂⁻⁻¹[Φ,∂⁻Φ]) + … . The twistor incidence relation guarantees that the non‑local inverse derivative ∂⁻⁻¹ is represented by a simple pole in the π‑plane, reproducing the canonical light‑front propagator.

When interactions are turned on, the light‑front Hamiltonian acquires higher‑point vertices that are precisely the MHV vertices of the twistor‑string construction. The equivalence can be shown by performing a canonical transformation on the twistor fields that removes the non‑local ∂⁻⁻¹ from the kinetic term and transfers it into the interaction vertices. The resulting Hamiltonian is a sum of local operators in the transverse plane, each multiplied by a factor of 1/p⁺ that is encoded in the twistor measure d²π/π̄π. This structure underlies the modern on‑shell recursion relations: the BCFW shift corresponds to a deformation of the real structure τ that moves the contour in the π‑plane, and the factorisation of the Hamiltonian on multi‑particle poles reproduces the BCFW recursion at the level of the light‑front S‑matrix.

Twistor Description of the Conformal Anomaly in Twistor‑String Worldsheet Theory

Witten’s twistor‑string is a topological B‑model on the super‑twistor space ℂℙ³|⁴ with target space the Calabi‑Yau super‑manifold. The worldsheet theory possesses a holomorphic stress tensor T(z) whose central charge receives contributions from the bosonic βγ system (c = 2), the fermionic bc system (c = −26), and the four fermionic ψ fields (c = 4). The total central charge vanishes only when the target space has complex dimension three and the fermionic directions are four, which is precisely the case for ℂℙ³|⁴. This cancellation is the twistor‑space avatar of the critical dimension condition for the superstring.

The conformal anomaly manifests in twistor space as a failure of the BRST operator Q to be nilpotent unless the target space satisfies the Calabi‑Yau condition c₁ = 0. In the language of sheaf cohomology, the anomaly is the obstruction class in H²(ℂℙ³|⁴, 𝒪) that must vanish for the quantum theory to be consistent. For the open twistor‑string the boundary conditions are given by D‑branes wrapping holomorphic cycles; the anomaly inflow from the bulk cancels the boundary anomaly only when the D‑brane configuration corresponds to a holomorphic Chern‑Simons theory on a space‑filling D5‑brane. This is the origin of the N = 4 super‑Yang‑Mills gauge theory that lives on the D5‑brane worldvolume.

At one loop the worldsheet partition function on a genus‑g Riemann surface computes the g‑loop amplitude of N = 4 SYM. The modular integral over the worldsheet moduli space reproduces the known planar amplitudes, while the non‑planar sectors arise from summing over different D‑brane Chan‑Paton factors. The conformal anomaly also controls the holomorphic anomaly equation of Bershadsky‑Cecotti‑Ooguri‑Vafa type: the anti‑holomorphic derivative of the amplitude with respect to the complex structure moduli of ℂℙ³|⁴ is given by a sum over boundary contributions where the worldsheet degenerates. In twistor space this equation becomes a statement about the variation of the twistor‑space amplitude under deformations of the complex structure of the target, linking the anomaly to the geometry of the amplituhedron boundaries.

Worked Example: Light‑Front Hamiltonian from Twistor Action
Starting from the twistor action S = ∫ d⁴x d⁸θ ℒ(Φ) with ℒ = ½ Φ □ Φ + g Φ³, derive the light‑front Hamiltonian density ℋ in terms of the twistor field Φ(π,π̄) on the null plane x⁺ = 0.
On the null plane the incidence relation reduces to ω^A = i x⁻ π^A, so the twistor field depends only on πA′ and x⁻. The kinetic term ∫ d⁴x Φ □ Φ becomes ∫ dx⁻ d²x⊥ d²π π̄π Φ ∂⁺∂⁻Φ. Since ∂⁺ = ∂/∂x⁺ generates translations in x⁺, the canonical momentum conjugate to Φ is Π = ∂⁻Φ. The Hamiltonian density is ℋ = Π ∂⁺Φ − ℒ = ½ (∂⁻Φ)² + g Φ³. Re‑expressing ∂⁻Φ in twistor variables gives ∂⁻Φ = ∫ d²π′ π̄′π′ Φ(π′) δ²(π−π′), which yields the non‑local kernel 1/p⁺. The final light‑front Hamiltonian is H = ∫ dx⁻ d²x⊥ [½ (∂⁻Φ)² + g Φ³] with the understanding that ∂⁻⁻¹ is represented by the twistor pole 1/(π̄π). This matches the known light‑front Hamiltonian of φ³ theory and shows how the twistor incidence relation encodes the light‑front propagator.
Exam‑Day Strategy
When a question asks for the light‑front Hamiltonian in twistor language, first write the incidence relation on the null plane, identify the dynamical twistor variables (π,π̄), and then perform the Legendre transform keeping the twistor measure d²π/π̄π explicit. The non‑local 1/p⁺ factor always appears as the residue of the π‑pole; do not attempt to invert ∂⁻ in position space.

Twistor Space of Anti‑de Sitter Space and the Holographic Dictionary

Anti‑de Sitter space AdSd+1 can be realised as a hyperboloid in ℝd,2. Its conformal boundary is a d‑dimensional Minkowski (or Euclidean) space on which the dual CFT lives. The twistor space of AdSd+1 is the space of null geodesics in the embedding space, which is isomorphic to the projective space of pure spinors in the conformal group SO(d,2). For AdS₅ the twistor space is the complex manifold ℂℙ³|⁴ with a real structure τ that picks out the AdS real slice; the boundary CFT twistor space is the same ℂℙ³|⁴ but with a different real structure τ_∂ corresponding to the Minkowski boundary.

The holographic dictionary in twistor language states that a bulk field of mass m and spin s corresponds to a cohomology class in H¹(ℂℙ³|⁴, 𝒪(k)) where k = −2h−2 and h is the helicity. The bulk‑to‑boundary propagator is the integral kernel that maps a boundary twistor function f(Z) to a bulk twistor function Φ(Z) by integrating over the boundary cycle defined by τ_∂. For a scalar field of dimension Δ the kernel is K(Z,Z_∂) = ⟨Z Z_∂⟩−Δ, where the bracket is the SL(4|4) invariant pairing. This reproduces the standard AdS/CFT bulk‑to‑boundary propagator after performing the Penrose transform to space‑time.

At the level of amplitudes, the tree‑level Witten diagrams in AdS become integrals over the moduli space of holomorphic curves in twistor space that end on the boundary cycle. The cubic vertex of a bulk scalar is represented by a degree‑one curve (a line) in ℂℙ³|⁴ intersecting the boundary at three points. The integral over the line’s moduli yields the standard Mellin‑space representation of the AdS three‑point function. Loop corrections correspond to higher‑genus curves with boundary components; the sum over genera reproduces the 1/N expansion of the boundary CFT. The twistor formulation makes the conformal symmetry manifest: the SL(4|4) invariance of the twistor action is precisely the super‑conformal symmetry of the dual N = 4 SYM theory.

Twistor Methods for the Non‑Perturbative Definition of the S‑Matrix via the Analytic Bootstrap

The analytic S‑matrix bootstrap seeks to determine scattering amplitudes solely from unitarity, crossing symmetry, analyticity, and polynomial boundedness. In twistor space these principles acquire a geometric formulation. Unitarity S†S = 1 translates into the statement that the twistor amplitude A(Z₁,…,Zₙ) satisfies a cutting rule: the discontinuity across a physical pole equals the product of lower‑point amplitudes integrated over the on‑shell phase space. In momentum‑twistor variables the phase‑space integral becomes a contour integral over the positive Grassmannian G₊(k,n), and the cutting rule is the factorisation of the canonical form of the amplituhedron on its boundaries.

Crossing symmetry — the analytic continuation from the s‑channel to the t‑channel — corresponds to a cluster mutation in the Grassmannian cluster algebra that exchanges the frozen variables associated with the two channels. The Mandelstam invariants sij = ⟨i j i+1 j+1⟩ are the cluster variables, and crossing is the mutation that changes the triangulation of the amplituhedron. Polynomial boundedness (the Froissart‑Martin bound) becomes the condition that the twistor amplitude has at most polynomial growth in the kinematic invariants, which in positive geometry means the canonical form has logarithmic singularities only on the boundaries of the amplituhedron, not in its interior.

The dispersion relations that express the amplitude in terms of its discontinuities become the BCFW recursion relations in twistor space. BCFW recursion is the statement that the canonical form of the amplituhedron can be triangulated by a sequence of BCFW shifts. For 2 → 2 scattering of identical scalars in a theory with a mass gap, the bootstrap reduces to a single‑variable problem for the cross‑ratio u = ⟨1234⟩²/(⟨1234⟩⟨3412⟩). The bootstrap equations are a set of integral equations for the discontinuity of A(u) across the cuts u ∈ [0,1] and u ∈ [1,∞). Recent work has shown that the solution space of these equations is in one‑to‑one correspondence with the space of consistent amplituhedron geometries, providing a non‑perturbative definition of the S‑matrix that does not rely on a Lagrangian.

Twistor Geometry of Supergravity Backgrounds with Ramond–Ramond Fluxes

The extension of the Penrose–Ward correspondence to type II supergravity requires a twistor space that encodes both the Neveu–Schwarz three‑form H and the Ramond–Ramond (RR) field strengths. In ten dimensions the relevant twistor space is a Calabi–Yau super‑manifold of dimension 3|4 fibered over a six‑dimensional base equipped with a pure spinor structure. The RR fluxes appear as cohomology classes in the sheaf of holomorphic differential forms on the twistor space, and the Bianchi identities for the fluxes translate into the Maurer–Cartan equations for a differential graded Lie algebra controlling deformations of the complex structure. A key result is that a type IIB background with only RR five‑form flux corresponds to a deformation of the standard twistor space ℂℙ³|⁴ by a closed (0,2)‑form representing the self‑dual five‑form. The integrability condition for the deformed complex structure is precisely the type IIB supergravity equation of motion for the five‑form. For backgrounds with non‑zero three‑form fluxes the twistor space acquires a non‑trivial holomorphic vector bundle whose Atiyah class encodes the H‑flux. The Penrose transform then maps Dolbeault cohomology groups of this bundle to solutions of the linearised supergravity equations on the space‑time. This construction has been used to generate explicit solutions such as the D3‑brane and the Klebanov–Strassler throat by solving the twistor equations on appropriate Calabi–Yau cones. The formalism also makes manifest the S‑duality of type IIB: the SL(2,ℤ) action on the RR and NS‑NS fluxes is realised as a group of automorphisms of the twistor space preserving the holomorphic symplectic form.

In practical calculations the twistor description reduces the problem of finding supersymmetric backgrounds to solving a set of holomorphic Chern–Simons equations on the twistor space. The fields of the Chern–Simons theory are a (0,1)‑connection on a holomorphic vector bundle and a (0,2)‑form representing the RR fluxes. The equations of motion are the vanishing of the (0,2)‑component of the curvature and the Bianchi identity for the (0,2)‑form. Solutions are in one‑to‑one correspondence with supersymmetric solutions of type IIB supergravity modulo gauge transformations. This equivalence has been proven for backgrounds preserving at least eight supercharges. For less supersymmetric backgrounds the twistor equations acquire higher‑order corrections that correspond to α′ corrections in the space‑time theory. The twistor approach therefore provides a systematic framework for incorporating stringy corrections into the geometry of supersymmetric backgrounds.

Twistor Description of the Euclidean Schwarzschild Instanton and its Moduli Space

The Euclidean Schwarzschild solution is a gravitational instanton with topology ℝ² × S² and a bolt singularity at the horizon. Its twistor space can be constructed by applying the Euclidean non‑linear graviton construction to a hyper‑Kähler manifold with a tri‑holomorphic U(1) action. The twistor space is a complex three‑fold fibred over ℂℙ¹ with fibres that are the twistor lines of the hyper‑Kähler metric. The real structure τ on the twistor space is induced by the antipodal map on the base ℂℙ¹ combined with complex conjugation on the fibres. The fixed point set of τ is a real three‑dimensional submanifold that corresponds to the bolt. The Penrose transform for this twistor space maps cohomology classes in H¹(𝒪(−2)) to linearised gravitational perturbations around the instanton. The moduli space of the instanton is captured by the deformation theory of the twistor space: infinitesimal deformations of the complex structure preserving the real structure and the fibration structure are parameterised by H¹(𝒪(−4)). This group is one‑dimensional, reflecting the single modulus — the mass parameter — of the Euclidean Schwarzschild solution. The twistor construction also yields the explicit form of the self‑dual Weyl spinor on the instanton, which is a section of the bundle 𝒪(−4) over the twistor space. The integral of this spinor over a twistor line reproduces the mass of the instanton via a twistor‑space version of the Komar integral. Higher‑genus corrections to the twistor space correspond to multi‑instanton configurations; the gluing of twistor spaces along common regions implements the ADHM‑type construction for gravitational instantons. The twistor description thus provides a geometric realisation of the moduli space of Euclidean Schwarzschild instantons as a complex manifold with a natural Kähler metric induced from the L² metric on the space of harmonic forms.

Worked Example: Mass from Twistor Cohomology
Show that the mass M of the Euclidean Schwarzschild instanton can be extracted from the twistor cohomology class in H¹(𝒪(−4)) by evaluating the contour integral ∮_C ω where ω is a representative (0,1)‑form with values in 𝒪(−4) and C is a contour encircling the bolt in the twistor space.
The twistor space Z of the Euclidean Schwarzschild instanton is a ℂℙ¹‑bundle over ℂℙ¹ with a real structure τ. The sheaf 𝒪(−4) on Z restricts to 𝒪(−4) on each twistor line L ≅ ℂℙ¹. A class [ω] ∈ H¹(Z, 𝒪(−4)) can be represented by a Čech cocycle ω01 on the overlap of two standard affine patches U₀, U₁ covering the base ℂℙ¹. On each patch the fibration is trivial, so ω01 is a homogeneous polynomial of degree −4 in the fibre coordinates. The contour C is taken in the base ℂℙ¹ around the point corresponding to the bolt. The integral ∮_C ω01 computes the residue of the cocycle at that point. By the Penrose transform, this residue equals the coefficient of the 1/r term in the asymptotic expansion of the metric, which is precisely 2M. Therefore M = (1/2) ∮_C ω01. The calculation matches the standard ADM mass formula and demonstrates that the mass modulus is encoded in the twistor cohomology group H¹(𝒪(−4)).
Exam Strategy
When a question asks for a physical parameter from twistor cohomology, identify the relevant sheaf (often 𝒪(k) with k negative), write down the Čech representative on the standard cover, and evaluate the contour integral around the real‑structure fixed points. The residue gives the parameter directly without solving the space‑time field equations.

Twistor Methods for the Classification of Supersymmetric Solutions in Five Dimensions

Five‑dimensional minimal supergravity admits a twistor description based on a six‑dimensional twistor space that is a ℂℙ¹‑bundle over a four‑dimensional base equipped with an almost complex structure. The supersymmetry conditions for a bosonic background (metric, gauge field) are equivalent to the existence of a covariantly constant spinor, which in turn is equivalent to the existence of a holomorphic section of a certain line bundle over the twistor space. The classification programme proceeds by analysing the geometry of the base: if the base admits a Kähler structure the solutions are the supersymmetric Gödel‑type universes and the BMPV black hole; if the base is hyper‑Kähler the solutions include the supersymmetric black rings and multi‑center solutions. The twistor space for a hyper‑Kähler base is a complex three‑fold with a holomorphic symplectic form, and the gauge field is encoded in a holomorphic line bundle with connection whose curvature is the pull‑back of the hyper‑Kähler triplet. The moduli space of supersymmetric solutions is then identified with the space of holomorphic line bundles on the twistor space satisfying a stability condition. This space carries a natural hyper‑Kähler metric induced from the L² metric on the space of harmonic forms, reproducing the known metric on the moduli space of multi‑center solutions. The twistor approach also clarifies the role of the bubble equations: they arise as the condition that the first Chern class of the line bundle restricts trivially to the exceptional divisors introduced by blowing up the twistor space at the locations of the centers. For non‑hyper‑Kähler bases the twistor space acquires a non‑trivial almost complex structure, and the classification reduces to solving a Monge–Ampère equation on the base. Recent work has shown that all known supersymmetric solutions of five‑dimensional minimal supergravity fit into this twistor framework, and the method has been extended to matter‑coupled supergravity by replacing the line bundle with a holomorphic vector bundle of higher rank.

Twistor Geometry of the Null Cone in Conformal Compactifications

The conformal compactification of Minkowski space adds a null cone ℐ (scri) at infinity. In twistor theory this boundary corresponds to the set of twistors that are incident with points on ℐ. The twistor space of the compactified Minkowski space is the projective twistor space ℂℙ³ with a real structure τ that has a five‑dimensional fixed point set — the null cone ℐ. The incidence relation for a point on ℐ becomes degenerate: the corresponding α‑plane is tangent to ℐ and its intersection with ℐ is a null line. This degeneracy is reflected in the twistor space by the fact that the fibres of the projection from the correspondence space to ℐ are one‑dimensional rather than two‑dimensional. The Penrose transform for fields on ℐ maps cohomology groups on the twistor space with support on the real slice to solutions of the conformal field equations on ℐ. In particular, the radiative data for massless fields (the news function) is encoded in the cohomology group H¹(ℐ, 𝒪(−2)) which is isomorphic to a subspace of H¹(ℂℙ³, 𝒪(−2)) consisting of classes that vanish on the real slice. The BMS group acts on ℐ as the group of conformal transformations preserving the null cone; its action lifts to the twistor space as the group of holomorphic automorphisms commuting with τ and preserving the fibration over ℐ. The supertranslation subgroup corresponds to the addition of a holomorphic function on the twistor space that is constant along the fibres over ℐ. This twistor picture provides a clean geometric derivation of the Bondi mass loss formula: the mass aspect is the coefficient of the 1/r term in the asymptotic expansion of the metric, which in twistor language is the residue of a certain meromorphic one‑form on the twistor space. The formula then follows from the residue theorem applied to a contour encircling the real slice. The same construction works for the conformal compactification of de Sitter space, where the null cone is replaced by a spacelike ℐ⁺ and the real structure on the twistor space changes accordingly.

Twistor Theory and the Geometry of the Light‑Cone Gauge in Momentum Twistor Space

Momentum twistors provide a parametrisation of the on‑shell kinematics of massless particles in four dimensions that makes dual conformal symmetry manifest. The light‑cone gauge in this language corresponds to fixing a reference twistor Z_* and requiring that all external momentum twistors Z_i satisfy ⟨Z_* Z_i⟩ = 1. This gauge choice removes the GL(1) redundancy of the momentum twistor variables and reduces the integration contour for loop amplitudes to a cycle in the positive Grassmannian G₊(k,n) that is invariant under the stabiliser of Z_*. The geometry of this gauge fixing is best understood by embedding the momentum twistor space into the projective space ℂℙ³ and considering the hyperplane H_* defined by ⟨Z_*·⟩ = 0. The condition ⟨Z_* Z_i⟩ = 1 means that the points Z_i lie on the affine chart complementary to H_*. The loop integrand for planar N = 4 SYM in the light‑cone gauge becomes a rational differential form on the configuration space of n points in this affine chart, with logarithmic singularities on the boundaries where any subset of points becomes collinear or coplanar. These boundaries are precisely the facets of the momentum amplituhedron. The BCFW recursion relations in momentum twistor space are generated by shifting two adjacent twistors Z_i → Z_i + z Z_j while preserving the gauge condition; this is possible only if the reference twistor Z_* is chosen generically. The shift corresponds to a mutation in the cluster algebra of the Grassmannian, and the recursion terminates when the shifted twistors hit the hyperplane H_*. The light‑cone gauge thus provides a geometric realisation of the cluster structure of the amplituhedron: each cluster chart corresponds to a choice of reference twistor, and cluster mutations correspond to changes of gauge. This perspective has been used to prove the all‑loop positivity of the planar integrand and to derive the symbol alphabet for multi‑loop amplitudes directly from the geometry of the hyperplane arrangement in ℂℙ³.

The twistor framework continues to unify diverse aspects of gravity, gauge theory, and integrable systems through a common geometric language.

The Classical Double Copy in Twistor Space: Kerr‑Schild Solutions and the Weyl Double Copy

The classical double copy asserts that certain exact solutions of Einstein's equations can be obtained by "squaring" solutions of Yang–Mills theory. In twistor language this correspondence becomes geometric: a self‑dual Yang–Mills field on spacetime corresponds to a holomorphic vector bundle on twistor space via the Ward correspondence, while a self‑dual gravitational field corresponds to a deformation of the complex structure of twistor space (the non‑linear graviton). The Kerr‑Schild ansatz gμν = ημν + Φ kμkν, with k a null geodesic vector field, provides a linearising map from a scalar field Φ on Minkowski space to an exact vacuum metric. In twistor space the Kerr‑Schild scalar Φ is encoded as a cohomology class in H¹(ℙ𝕋, 𝒪(−2)) satisfying a quadratic constraint that is precisely the condition for the deformed twistor space to admit a global holomorphic section of the canonical bundle. The Weyl double copy refines this: the Weyl spinor ΨABCD of the gravity solution is the symmetrised product of two Yang–Mills field strengths FAB and F̃CD (or two copies of the same field for the single copy). On twistor space this translates to the statement that the deformation of the complex structure is generated by a Hamiltonian vector field whose symbol is the product of two holomorphic functions representing the gauge fields. For the Kerr solution the relevant Yang–Mills field is the Coulomb field of a point charge; its twistor representative is a meromorphic function with a simple pole on the real slice. The product of two such functions yields the quadratic pole structure that characterises the Kerr twistor space. This construction extends to the Kerr–Newman and Taub–NUT solutions, and to the multi‑center Gibbons–Hawking metrics where the Yang–Mills side becomes a collection of Dirac monopoles. The twistor formulation makes manifest why the double copy works for algebraically special spacetimes: the Petrov type D condition is equivalent to the factorisation of the Weyl spinor, which in twistor terms means the deformation Hamiltonian factorises into two linear factors.

Twistor Theory and the Infrared Structure of Scattering Amplitudes: Soft Theorems, Memory Effects, and the Celestial Sphere

Infrared divergences in gauge theory and gravity are governed by universal soft theorems that relate an n+1‑particle amplitude with a soft photon or graviton to the n‑particle amplitude multiplied by a universal soft factor. In twistor space these theorems acquire a geometric interpretation: a soft particle corresponds to a puncture on the worldsheet of the twistor string that approaches the boundary of the moduli space. The soft factor is the residue of the worldsheet current at that puncture. For gravity the leading soft graviton theorem is equivalent to the Ward identity of the BMS supertranslation symmetry at null infinity ℐ. The twistor space of asymptotically flat spacetimes fibres over ℐ, and the BMS group acts as holomorphic automorphisms preserving the fibration. A supertranslation is generated by a function on the celestial sphere; its action on the twistor space is the addition of a holomorphic function constant along the fibres. The gravitational memory effect — the permanent displacement of test particles after a burst of gravitational radiation — is the Fourier transform of the soft graviton theorem. In twistor language the memory is encoded in the asymptotic behaviour of the twistor connection along the real slice: the difference between the retarded and advanced twistor connections at ℐ⁺ and ℐ⁻ is a cohomology class in H¹(ℐ, 𝒪(−2)) that measures the net supertranslation charge. The subleading soft graviton theorem corresponds to the superrotation symmetry, which acts on the celestial sphere as a local conformal transformation. Its twistor realisation involves the action of vector fields on the twistor space that do not preserve the fibration over ℐ but instead deform the complex structure of the fibres. The celestial holography programme recasts the four‑dimensional S‑matrix as a correlation function of operators on the celestial sphere. In twistor space this is the statement that the scattering amplitude is the partition function of a two‑dimensional conformal field theory living on the celestial sphere, with the twistor string providing the worldsheet description. The soft theorems become Ward identities of the celestial CFT, and the memory effect is the expectation value of the celestial stress tensor.

Worked Example: Soft Graviton Theorem from Twistor Residue
Derive the leading soft graviton factor for an n‑particle MHV amplitude in planar N = 4 SYM coupled to gravity using the twistor‑string worldsheet. Show that the factor matches the universal Weinberg soft factor.
In the twistor‑string the MHV amplitude is supported on a degree‑1 worldsheet instanton, a holomorphic map Σ → ℙ𝕋 of degree 1. A soft graviton of momentum k and helicity +2 corresponds to inserting a vertex operator V+2(k) = ∫Σ d²z ei k·X(z) h++(z) where h++ is the graviton wavefunction. In the soft limit k → 0 the exponential expands to 1 + i k·X + …; the constant term vanishes by momentum conservation. The linear term gives ∫Σ d²z k·X(z) h++(z). On the degree‑1 instanton the embedding coordinates Xμ(z) are linear in the worldsheet coordinate, and the integral localises to the puncture where the soft graviton is inserted. Evaluating the residue yields ∑i=1n k·pi / k·pi × (helicity factor) = ∑i εμν+(k) piμ piν / k·pi, which is precisely the Weinberg soft graviton factor. The twistor derivation makes the universality manifest: the factor depends only on the external hard momenta and the soft polarisation, not on the details of the hard amplitude.

When a question asks for the origin of a soft theorem, always identify the asymptotic symmetry (BMS supertranslation for leading soft graviton, superrotation for subleading). In twistor language the symmetry acts on the twistor space as a holomorphic automorphism preserving the real slice. The soft factor is the Noether charge of that symmetry evaluated on the scattering state. This symmetry‑based answer scores higher than a purely algebraic derivation.

The Regge Limit and High‑Energy Scattering in Twistor Space: The BFKL Pomeron and the Twistor Description of Reggeization

The Regge limit of a scattering amplitude — centre‑of‑mass energy s → ∞ with fixed momentum transfer t — is dominated by the exchange of a Regge pole, the Pomeron in QCD. In planar N = 4 SYM the BFKL equation resums leading logarithms of s and determines the Pomeron intercept. Twistor space provides a natural framework for this limit because the high‑energy kinematics corresponds to a configuration where two sets of external twistors become nearly collinear in a specific sense. In momentum twistor space the Regge limit is realised by taking two adjacent momentum twistors Zi, Zi+1 to approach a common line in ℂℙ³ while the remaining twistors stay generic. The BFKL kernel then acts on the space of functions of the cross‑ratios formed from the four‑brackets of the momentum twistors. The eigenvalue equation for the Pomeron becomes a spectral problem for an integrable Hamiltonian — the Lipatov Hamiltonian — which in twistor language is the generator of holomorphic diffeomorphisms of the twistor space preserving the incidence relations for the Regge kinematics. The eigenfunctions are the conformal three‑point functions of the celestial CFT, and the eigenvalues give the anomalous dimensions of the leading‑twist operators. At strong coupling the AdS/CFT correspondence maps the Regge limit to the eikonal scattering of strings in AdS₅, which in twistor space is described by the classical string worldsheet ending on the celestial sphere. The Pomeron intercept at strong coupling is determined by the minimal area of a string worldsheet in the AdS bulk, which via the twistor correspondence becomes a minimal surface in the twistor space of AdS₅. The twistor formulation also clarifies the relation between the BFKL Pomeron and the double logarithmic limit (DGLAP): the former resums logs of s, the latter resums logs of Q²; in twistor space they correspond to different degenerations of the configuration of external twistors — collinear for DGLAP, multi‑Regge for BFKL. The recent derivation of the BFKL equation from the twistor‑string at one loop confirms that the Regge limit is captured by the boundary of the moduli space of the worldsheet where a handle pinches, separating the amplitude into two clusters connected by a Reggeised gluon.

Twistor Geometry of Hyper‑Kähler and Quaternionic Kähler Manifolds: The Swann Bundle, the c‑Map, and the Twistor Space of the Hyper‑Kähler Cone

A hyper‑Kähler manifold M of real dimension 4n admits a 2‑sphere of complex structures. Its twistor space Z is a ℂℙ¹‑bundle over M whose fibre over x ∈ M parametrises the complex structures. Z carries a natural holomorphic contact structure and a real structure τ covering the antipodal map on ℂℙ¹. The Swann construction associates to M a hyper‑Kähler cone C(M) = M × ℝ⁺ with a homothetic Killing vector. The twistor space of C(M) is the total space of the line bundle 𝒪(2) over Z minus the zero section; the homothety acts as fibre scaling. For a quaternionic Kähler manifold Q of dimension 4n (positive scalar curvature) the twistor space is a ℂℙ¹‑bundle with a Kähler–Einstein metric and a contact structure. The c‑map relates the moduli space of hyper‑multiplets in N = 2 supergravity (a quaternionic Kähler manifold) to the moduli space of vector multiplets (a special Kähler manifold). In twistor language the c‑map is realised by a Legendre transform on the twistor space: the contact potential on the quaternionic Kähler twistor space is the Legendre dual of the Kähler potential on the special Kähler base. The hyper‑Kähler cone over the quaternionic Kähler manifold is the total space of the Swann bundle, and its twistor space is the 𝒪(2) bundle over the quaternionic Kähler twistor space. This construction underlies the twistor description of the hyper‑multiplet moduli space in type II string theory compactified on a Calabi–Yau threefold: the perturbative metric is the c‑map of the special Kähler moduli space of the Calabi–Yau, and non‑perturbative corrections (D‑instantons, NS5‑branes) are encoded as deformations of the contact structure on the twistor space. The twistor space thus provides a unified geometric framework for both perturbative and non‑perturbative quantum corrections to the hyper‑multiplet metric.

Twistor Theory and the Non‑Perturbative S‑Matrix: The Analytic Bootstrap and the Twistor Description of Bound States

The analytic bootstrap programme seeks to determine the S‑matrix of a quantum field theory from its analytic properties — unitarity, crossing symmetry, and the spectrum of bound states — without relying on a Lagrangian. Twistor theory enters because the analytic structure of scattering amplitudes in planar N = 4 SYM is exceptionally simple: the amplitude is a rational function of momentum twistors with only logarithmic singularities on the boundaries of the positive Grassmannian. The non‑perturbative completion requires summing over all genera of the twistor‑string worldsheet, which corresponds to summing over all topologies of the on‑shell diagrams. The resulting object is a section of a line bundle over the moduli space of curves with marked points, satisfying a set of Riemann–Hilbert type monodromy conditions that encode unitarity. Bound states appear as poles in the complex angular momentum plane (Regge poles). In twistor space a bound state corresponds to a holomorphic curve in the twistor space that is not a degree‑1 instanton but a higher‑degree curve with non‑trivial normal bundle. The residue at the pole is the product of the couplings of the bound state to the external particles, which in twistor language are the evaluation maps of the curve at the marked points. The analytic bootstrap equations become consistency conditions for the gluing of these higher‑degree curves along their boundaries. For integrable theories the bootstrap closes on a finite set of particles, and the twistor space is a rational variety whose geometry encodes the factorised S‑matrix. The recent formulation of the S‑matrix bootstrap in twistor space for the O(N) sigma model shows that the crossing equations are equivalent to the associativity of a certain star product on the space of functions on the twistor space, providing a direct link between the analytic bootstrap and the deformation quantisation of the twistor Poisson structure.

Twistor Theory and the Seiberg–Witten Geometry of N = 2 Supersymmetric Gauge Theories

The exact solution of N = 2 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory by Seiberg and Witten is naturally formulated in the language of twistor geometry. The Coulomb branch of the theory is a special Kähler manifold whose metric is encoded in a holomorphic prepotential F(a). The central charge of a BPS state with electric–magnetic charges (ne, nm) is Z = ne a + nm aD, where aD = ∂F/∂a. The Seiberg–Witten curve Σu : y2 = (x2 − Λ4)(x − u) is a family of elliptic curves fibered over the u‑plane. The periods of the Seiberg–Witten differential λ = x dy/y give a and aD. In twistor terms the total space of the fibration Σ → ℂu is the twistor space of the hyperkähler moduli space of vacua. Each point of the base corresponds to a twistor line ℂℙ1 in the twistor space, and the holomorphic symplectic form Ω = da ∧ daD extends to a holomorphic section of 𝒪(2) over the twistor ℂℙ1. The BPS spectrum is recovered from the intersection numbers of these twistor lines with the discriminant locus where the curve degenerates. Wall‑crossing phenomena are described by the Kontsevich–Soibelman symplectomorphisms acting on the torus fibers of the twistor space, which coincide with the mutations of the cluster algebra associated to the quiver of the theory. The construction generalises to arbitrary gauge groups via the Hitchin system: the moduli space of Higgs bundles on a Riemann surface C is hyperkähler, its twistor space is the moduli space of flat SL(2,ℂ) connections on C × ℂℙ1, and the Seiberg–Witten differential becomes the canonical one‑form on the spectral curve. This twistor picture underlies the geometric engineering of N = 2 theories in string theory and provides a uniform framework for the computation of instanton corrections to the prepotential via the topological string partition function on the associated Calabi–Yau threefold.

Twistor Methods for Wilson Loops and Correlation Functions in Planar N = 4 SYM

The duality between planar scattering amplitudes and light‑like polygonal Wilson loops in N = 4 SYM is most transparent in momentum twistor space. A null polygon with vertices xi is mapped to a sequence of momentum twistors Zi = (λi, μi) satisfying μi = xi λi. The expectation value of the Wilson loop Wn depends only on the dual conformal cross‑ratios ui = (Zi Zi+1 Zi+2 Zi+3)/(Zi Zi+1 Zi+3 Zi+4). For MHV configurations the loop integrand is a rational function of the Zi with only logarithmic singularities on the boundaries of the positive Grassmannian G+(k,n). The amplituhedron construction identifies the integrand with a canonical differential form on a positive geometry inside G(k,n). At NMHV and higher the same geometry yields the ratio function Rn,k = An,k/An,MHV, which satisfies a set of first‑order differential equations (the symbol bootstrap) whose alphabet consists of the Plücker coordinates ⟨i j k l⟩. Correlation functions of half‑BPS operators Ok = Tr(φk) are similarly encoded: the three‑point function ⟨Ok1 Ok2 Ok3⟩ is a polynomial in the twistor brackets, and the four‑point function can be expanded in conformal blocks whose coefficients are given by the same positive Grassmannian integrals. The hexagon bootstrap for the fishnet limit of the theory shows that the integrability of the planar dilatation operator translates into a factorised S‑matrix for excitations on the worldsheet of the dual string, and the twistor representation makes the Yangian symmetry Y[psu(2,2|4)] manifest as a set of level‑one generators acting linearly on the Zi. Recent work has extended the twistor formalism to non‑planar corrections by introducing a genus expansion of the amplituhedron, where each handle corresponds to an additional integration over a pair of momentum twistors subject to the same positivity constraints.

Twistor Geometry of the AdS₃/CFT₂ Correspondence and the Symmetric Orbifold

The AdS3 × S3 × T4 (or K3) background with NS‑NS flux is described by a tensionless string whose worldsheet theory is a symmetric product orbifold CFT SymN(T4) in the large N limit. The twistor space of AdS3 is the complex manifold ℙ3|4 with a real structure that reduces to the conformal boundary cylinder ℝ × S1. Twistor Description of the Integrable Fishnet Theory and its Double‑Scaling Limit

The bi‑scalar fishnet theory arises as a double‑scaling limit of γ‑deformed N = 4 SYM where the gauge coupling g → 0 and the deformation parameter γ → i∞ while ξ = g eiγ is held fixed. This formalism reproduces the exact planar correlators at any loop order and provides a direct link between the fishnet integrability and the AdS5 × S5 string worldsheet S‑matrix.

Twistor Theory and the Conformal Bootstrap in Momentum Space: The Lorentzian Inversion Formula

The Lorentzian inversion formula of Caron‑Huot expresses the OPE data of a CFT four‑point function as an integral of the double discontinuity of the correlator over the Lorentzian region. In twistor language the conformal group SO(4,2) is isomorphic to SU(2,2), and its fundamental representation is the twistor space ℂ4. Momentum twistors Zi = (λi, μi) provide a parametrisation of the conformal cross‑ratios that linearises the action of the conformal group. The double discontinuity dDisc[G(u,v)] becomes a contour integral over the twistor variables of the product of two three‑point functions ⟨O O O⟩, each of which is a homogeneous polynomial in the twistor brackets. The inversion kernel K(u,v) is the twistor transform of the conformal Casimir eigenfunction, and its explicit form is a rational function of the Plücker coordinates ⟨i j k l⟩. The OPE coefficients cΔ,ℓ are then obtained by projecting the double discontinuity onto the basis of conformal blocks, which in twistor space are the harmonic functions on the Grassmannian Gr(2,4) with definite scaling dimension. This formulation makes the analytic structure of the OPE data manifest: the poles in the complex spin plane correspond to the twistor lines that intersect the singular locus of the correlator. The method has been applied to the 3D Ising model, where the twistor space is the Grassmannian Gr(2,3) ≅ ℂℙ2, and to planar N = 4 SYM, where the momentum twistor representation yields the exact all‑loop OPE data from the hexagonalisation of the fishnet graphs. The twistor inversion formula also clarifies the relation between the light‑cone bootstrap and the celestial bootstrap: the celestial sphere is the space of null directions in Minkowski space, which is precisely the projectivised twistor space ℙ3 modulo the real structure.

Twistor Geometry of the Moduli Space of Instantons on ALE Spaces and the McKay Correspondence

The moduli space of instantons on asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) spaces admits a twistor description that realises the McKay correspondence geometrically. An ALE space is a hyper‑Kähler four‑manifold asymptotic to ℝ⁴/Γ where Γ ⊂ SU(2) is a finite subgroup classified by the ADE Dynkin diagrams. The twistor space of an ALE space is a non‑compact complex three‑fold Z containing a distinguished rational curve ℂℙ¹ with normal bundle 𝒪(1)⊕𝒪(1), and the ADE singularity is resolved by a chain of ℂℙ¹s whose intersection matrix is the negative Cartan matrix of the corresponding Lie algebra. Instantons on the ALE space correspond, via the Penrose–Ward transform, to holomorphic vector bundles on Z that are trivial on the twistor lines. The ADHM construction for instantons on ℝ⁴ generalises to ALE spaces by replacing the vector spaces in the ADHM quiver with representations of Γ, yielding the Nakajima quiver variety description of the instanton moduli space. The twistor space Z fibres over ℂℙ¹ with fibres the ALE space, and the relative twistor transform identifies the moduli space of framed instantons with the moduli space of holomorphic bundles on Z satisfying a framing condition at infinity. The McKay correspondence appears as the isomorphism between the equivariant K‑theory of the instanton moduli space and the representation ring of the affine Kac–Moody algebra associated to the ADE diagram. The twistor description makes the hyper‑Kähler structure of the moduli space manifest: the three complex structures arise from the ℂℙ¹ base of the twistor fibration, and the hyper‑Kähler metric is obtained by the twistor construction of Hitchin, Karlhede, Lindström and Roček. For the A₁ singularity (Eguchi–Hanson space), the twistor space is the total space of 𝒪(−2)⊕𝒪(−2) over ℂℙ¹ blown up at a point, and the instanton moduli space is the Hilbert scheme of points on the Eguchi–Hanson space. The twistor transform of the instanton connection yields a holomorphic bundle whose restriction to each twistor line is trivial, and the framing data at infinity encode the asymptotic holonomy. This framework extends to instantons on multi‑Taub–NUT spaces and to the moduli space of monopoles on ℝ³ via the hyper‑Kähler rotation that relates the ALE space to the moduli space of monopoles.

Twistor Methods for the Computation of Gravitational Waveforms and the Post‑Minkowskian Expansion

The post‑Minkowskian (PM) expansion of gravitational waveforms for binary black hole scattering admits a twistor formulation that organises the classical limit of scattering amplitudes by helicity and makes the double‑copy structure manifest. In the KMOC formalism, the classical waveform is extracted from the Fourier transform of the five‑point amplitude with two massive scalars and three gravitons. In momentum twistor space, the massive momenta are represented by pairs of twistors (Z, W) satisfying the incidence relation μ = xλ, and the graviton states are represented by twistor wavefunctions of helicity ±2. The PM expansion corresponds to an expansion in the gravitational coupling G, and at each order the amplitude is a sum over Feynman diagrams that localise on the support of the scattering equations in twistor space. The leading PM order (1PM) reproduces the linearised Kerr solution, and the twistor description of the Kerr black hole as a twistor‑space sheaf supported on a degree‑two curve in ℙ³ makes the Newman–Janis shift manifest. At 2PM, the amplitude involves the iteration of the three‑point vertex, and the twistor‑space integrand is a rational function of the Plücker coordinates ⟨i j k l⟩ with poles corresponding to the factorisation channels. The classical limit is taken by scaling the twistor variables with ℏ⁻¹/² and extracting the stationary phase contribution, which localises the twistor integrals on the classical solutions of the self‑dual gravity equations. The double copy in twistor space replaces the colour factors of the gauge theory amplitude with a second copy of the kinematic numerators, and the gravitational integrand is the product of two gauge theory integrands. The waveform at future null infinity ℐ⁺ is obtained by the Penrose transform of the twistor‑space field: the radiative component Ψ₄ is the twistor transform of a (0,1)‑form on ℙ³ with values in 𝒪(−6), and the memory effect corresponds to the non‑trivial topology of the twistor‑space sheaf at the boundary of the twistor space. The post‑Minkowskian expansion to 3PM and beyond has been computed using the twistor‑string inspired CHY formalism, where the scattering equations on the Riemann sphere are replaced by their twistor‑space counterparts, and the integration over the moduli space of punctured spheres is replaced by a contour integral over the Grassmannian Gr(2, n) in twistor space. This approach yields the classical observables — scattering angle, impulse, and waveform — directly from the twistor‑space data without passing through the effective field theory matching procedure.

Twistor Description of the Holographic Entanglement Entropy and the Ryu‑Takayanagi Formula

The Ryu‑Takayanagi formula for holographic entanglement entropy in AdS/CFT admits a twistor‑geometric interpretation that relates the minimal surface area in the bulk to a topological invariant of a twistor‑space cycle. In the AdS₅/CFT₄ correspondence, the bulk AdS₅ has a twistor space that is the projective spinor bundle ℙ(𝒪(1)⊕𝒪(1)) over ℂℙ³, or equivalently the flag manifold F(1,2;4) of lines in ℂ⁴. A boundary subregion A on the conformal boundary ℝ×S³ corresponds to a domain in the celestial twistor space ℙ³, and the Ryu‑Takayanagi surface γ_A is the minimal surface in AdS₅ homologous to A. The twistor correspondence maps γ_A to a holomorphic curve C_A in the twistor space of AdS₅, which is a section of the twistor fibration over γ_A. The area of γ_A is computed by the twistor‑space integral ∫C_A Ω ∧ ω, where Ω is the holomorphic volume form on the twistor space and ω is a Kähler form representing the hyper‑Kähler structure. For a spherical entangling surface in the vacuum state, the minimal surface is a hyperbolic plane H³ in AdS₅, and its twistor lift is a ℂℙ¹ bundle over H³. The area integral reduces to the volume of H³, which diverges as the UV cutoff ε → 0. The universal logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy for a CFT in four dimensions is proportional to the Euler characteristic of the entangling surface, and in twistor space this term arises from the intersection number of the twistor cycle C_A with the canonical divisor of the twistor space. For excited states, the minimal surface is deformed, and the twistor description incorporates the backreaction via the non‑linear graviton construction: the bulk metric perturbation corresponds to a deformation of the twistor space complex structure, and the change in the minimal surface area is computed by the variation of the twistor‑space period integral. The covariant Hubeny‑Rangamani‑Takayanagi prescription for time‑dependent states is realised in twistor space by allowing the twistor cycle C_A to be a complex chain with boundary on the celestial twistor space, and the area is the real part of the period integral. The quantum corrections to the Ryu‑Takayanagi formula (the Faulkner‑Lewkowycz‑Maldacena formula) correspond in twistor space to the genus expansion of the twistor‑string worldsheet: the bulk entanglement entropy of quantum fields is the sum over genera of the twistor‑string partition function with boundary conditions on C_A. The twistor formulation also clarifies the relation between entanglement entropy and the modular Hamiltonian: the modular flow is generated by a vector field on the twistor space that preserves the twistor cycle C_A, and the modular Hamiltonian is the twistor transform of the Noether charge associated to this symmetry.

Twistor Theory and the Geometry of the Non‑Local Charges in Integrable Sigma Models: The Yangian Symmetry

The Yangian symmetry of the two‑dimensional principal chiral model and the AdS₅×S⁵ superstring is realised geometrically in twistor space as the algebra of non‑local charges acting on the twistor‑space sheaves that correspond to the Lax connection. The twistor‑space realisation of the Yangian uses the fact that the super‑twistor space is a Calabi‑Yau supermanifold with a holomorphic volume form Ω. The Yangian generators are represented as contour integrals of Ω against certain (0,1)‑forms with values in the adjoint bundle. The coproduct of the Yangian corresponds to the gluing of twistor‑space cycles, and the R‑matrix is the twistor transform of the universal R‑matrix of the Yangian. The Bethe ansatz equations for the spectrum of the dilatation operator are derived by diagonalising the transfer matrix, which in twistor space is the holonomy of the Lax connection around the spatial circle. The quantum spectral curve, which encodes the exact spectrum at finite coupling, is a Riemann‑Hilbert problem on the twistor ℂℙ¹: the quasi‑momenta are the eigenvalues of the monodromy matrix, and their analytic structure is determined by the twistor‑space geometry of the Lax connection. The twistor description also explains the origin of the secret symmetry of the AdS₅×S⁵ S‑matrix: it is the remnant of the superconformal symmetry of the twistor space that is not manifest in the light‑cone gauge.

Twistor Geometry of Conformal Higher‑Spin Theories and the Twistor Action for Conformal Supergravity

Conformal higher‑spin (CHS) theories in four dimensions are naturally formulated in twistor space, where the infinite tower of higher‑spin fields is packaged into a single master field on the twistor space ℙ³. The twistor action also provides a generating functional for the conformal higher‑spin correlators: the n‑point functions are obtained by differentiating the partition function with respect to sources coupled to the master field, and the twistor‑space Feynman rules are remarkably simple — the propagator is the Green's function of the ∂̄‑operator on ℙ³, and the vertices are the structure constants of the higher‑spin algebra. The CHS theory is UV finite in four dimensions, and the twistor formulation makes this finiteness manifest: the twistor‑space integrals are convergent because the propagator falls off as |Z|⁻⁴ at infinity, and the vertices are polynomial in the twistor variables.

Twistor Description of the Steinmann Relations, Cluster Adjacency, and the Symbol Alphabet in Planar N=4 SYM

The Steinmann relations state that the double discontinuity of a scattering amplitude in overlapping momentum channels vanishes. The Steinmann relations then restrict the symbol to the Steinmann cluster algebra, a subalgebra of the full cluster algebra where only compatible pairs appear. This twistor‑geometric origin explains why the symbol alphabet is finite and why the amplitudes satisfy the extended Steinmann relations at all loop orders.
