Exam Strategy: Mukai Flop and Wall-Crossing
When a question asks about wall-crossing for a Mukai flop, identify the Mukai vector v and compute v2. If v2 = 2, the moduli space is a K3 surface and the flop is a classical flop. The wall in Stab corresponds to the hyperplane orthogonal to v in the period domain. The DT invariants are Euler characteristics of moduli spaces; for K3 surfaces they are constant (24) under flops. The key formula is the KS wall-crossing: ∏ Φ(y^γ)Ω(γ) is invariant. Remember that the Fourier-Mukai equivalence D^b(Coh(M)) ≅ D^b(Coh(S)) identifies Stab(M) with Stab(S), so wall-crossing on M is the same as wall-crossing on S for objects of class v.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Quiver Varieties and the Nakajima Construction

Let Q be a quiver with dimension vector v and framing vector w. The Nakajima quiver variety 𝔐_θ(v, w) is constructed as a GIT quotient of the representation space Rep(Q, v, w) by the group G_v = ∏_i GL(v_i) with stability parameter θ ∈ ℤQ0. The derived category D^b(Coh(𝔐_θ(v, w))) admits a stability condition constructed via the window subcategory method of Halpern-Leistner and Shipman. For a character χ: G_v → ℂ^*, the window subcategory 𝒲_χ ⊂ D^bG_v(Rep(Q, v, w)) is the full subcategory generated by objects whose weights lie in a certain interval. The derived category of the GIT quotient is equivalent to the window subcategory: D^b(Coh(𝔐_θ(v, w))) ≅ 𝒲_χ. A stability condition on D^b(Coh(𝔐_θ(v, w))) is induced by a stability condition on the equivariant derived category D^bG_v(Rep(Q, v, w)) that satisfies the support property with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group NG_v(Rep(Q, v, w)). The central charge takes the form Z(E) = ∑_i θ_i rank(E_i) + ∑_a m_a weight_a(E) where the sum is over vertices i and arrows a, and m_a are parameters determined by the Kähler form on the quiver variety. The space of stability conditions Stab^†(𝔐_θ(v, w)) has a connected component that is a covering of the space of stability parameters θ modulo the action of the Weyl group of the Kac-Moody algebra associated to Q. The walls in Stab^†(𝔐_θ(v, w)) correspond to the hyperplanes where θ·α = 0 for roots α of the Kac-Moody algebra. The DT invariants of 𝔐_θ(v, w) are the Euler characteristics of moduli spaces of stable objects, and they are related to the BPS invariants of the quiver with potential (Q, W) via the motivic Hall algebra. The cohomological Hall algebra (CoHA) of the quiver variety is isomorphic to the positive half of the quantum group U_q(𝔤_Q) where 𝔤_Q is the Kac-Moody algebra of Q. The integration map from the motivic Hall algebra to the quantum torus sends the class of a stable object to a quantum dilogarithm, and the wall-crossing formula is the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the quantum torus. For the Jordan quiver (one vertex, one loop) with framing w = 1, the quiver variety is the Hilbert scheme of points Hilb^n(ℂ2), and the stability conditions on D^b(Coh(Hilb^n(ℂ2))) are related to the stability conditions on the derived category of the resolved conifold via the crepant resolution conjecture.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Hypertoric Varieties and the Gale Duality

A hypertoric variety (or toric hyperkähler variety) 𝔐 is constructed as a hyperkähler quotient of a flat hyperkähler vector space by a torus action. Let T be a torus acting on ℍ^n = T^*ℂ^n with moment maps μ_ℝ: ℍ^n → 𝔱^* and μ_ℂ: ℍ^n → 𝔱^*_ℂ. The hypertoric variety is 𝔐 = μ_ℝ-1(α) ∩ μ_ℂ-1(β) / T for generic parameters α ∈ 𝔱^*, β ∈ 𝔱^*_ℂ. The derived category D^b(Coh(𝔐)) is equivalent to the derived category of modules over a hypertoric enveloping algebra, which is a deformation of the coordinate ring of the hypertoric variety. Stability conditions on D^b(Coh(𝔐)) are constructed via the Gale dual hypertoric variety 𝔐^!. The Gale duality exchanges the torus T with its dual T^! and the parameters (α, β) with (β, α). Under this duality, the derived category D^b(Coh(𝔐)) is equivalent to D^b(Coh(𝔐^!)) via a Fourier-Mukai type transform. The space of stability conditions Stab^†(𝔐) is isomorphic to Stab^†(𝔐^!) and both are coverings of the complement of a hyperplane arrangement in ℂ^d where d = dim 𝔐. The hyperplane arrangement is the Gale dual of the arrangement defining the toric variety associated to 𝔐. The central charge for a stability condition on D^b(Coh(𝔐)) takes the form Z(E) = ∑_i θ_i ch_i(E) where θ_i are the stability parameters and ch_i are the Chern characters with respect to a basis of the numerical Grothendieck group N(𝔐). The walls in Stab^†(𝔐) correspond to the hyperplanes where θ·v = 0 for v ∈ N(𝔐) the class of a spherical object. The DT invariants of 𝔐 are the Euler characteristics of moduli spaces of stable objects, and they are given by the coefficients of the generating function ∏γ Φ(y^γ)Ω(γ) where the product is over the positive roots of the hypertoric arrangement. The support property for stability conditions on D^b(Coh(𝔐)) is equivalent to the condition that the quadratic form Q(v) = -χ(v, v) is negative definite on the kernel of Z, where χ is the Euler pairing on N(𝔐). The numerical Grothendieck group N(𝔐) is isomorphic to the homology of the hypertoric variety, and the Euler pairing corresponds to the intersection pairing. For the hypertoric variety associated to the A_n arrangement, the space of stability conditions is a covering of the complement of the braid arrangement, and the monodromy action is given by the braid group.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Log Calabi-Yau Varieties and the Gross-Siebert Program

Let (X, D) be a log Calabi-Yau pair where X is a smooth projective variety and D ⊂ X is a simple normal crossings divisor such that K_X + D ∼ 0. The derived category D^b(Coh(X)) admits a stability condition constructed by gluing stability conditions on the strata of D. For each stratum D_I = ∩i∈I D_i, the derived category D^b(Coh(D_I)) has a stability condition induced by the restriction of a stability condition on D^b(Coh(X)). The central charge on D^b(Coh(X)) takes the form Z(E) = ∫_X e-B-iω ch(E) √td(X) + ∑_I c_I ∫D_I e-B_I-iω_I ch(E|D_I) where B, ω are the B-field and Kähler form on X, and B_I, ω_I are their restrictions to D_I. The coefficients c_I are determined by the log structure. The space of stability conditions Stab^†(X) contains a component that fibers over the product of Stab(D^b(Coh(D_I))) with fiber the space of gluing data. The Gross-Siebert program constructs the mirror of X as a degeneration of log Calabi-Yau varieties over a base B0, and the derived category of the mirror is related to D^b(Coh(X)) by a version of homological mirror symmetry for log Calabi-Yau varieties. The wall-crossing of stability conditions on D^b(Coh(X)) corresponds to the wall-crossing of scattering diagrams in the Gross-Siebert program. The DT invariants of X are the Euler characteristics of moduli spaces of stable objects, and they are related to the Gromov-Witten invariants of X via the DT/GW correspondence for log Calabi-Yau varieties. The motivic Hall algebra of D^b(Coh(X)) has a subalgebra generated by objects supported on the divisor D, and the integration map to the quantum torus sends this subalgebra to the scattering diagram algebra. The support property for stability conditions on D^b(Coh(X)) is equivalent to the condition that the quadratic form Q(v) = -χ(v, v) is negative definite on the kernel of Z, where χ is the Euler pairing on the numerical Grothendieck group N(X). For the pair (ℙ2, E) where E is a smooth cubic curve, the space of stability conditions Stab^†(ℙ2) has a component that is a covering of the complement of the discriminant locus in the space of cubic curves, and the walls correspond to the vanishing of the central charge on classes of objects supported on E.

  • Confusing the Nakajima quiver variety construction with the GIT quotient for quiver representations without framing; the framing vector w is essential for the hyperkähler structure and the symplectic resolution.
  • Assuming the space of stability conditions on a hypertoric variety is always connected; it is a covering of the complement of a hyperplane arrangement, which has multiple components corresponding to the chambers of the arrangement.
  • Treating the Gale dual hypertoric variety as the mirror in the sense of homological mirror symmetry; Gale duality is a derived equivalence but not necessarily the mirror symmetry equivalence, which involves the Fukaya category.
  • Neglecting the role of the log structure in stability conditions on log Calabi-Yau pairs; the central charge must include contributions from all strata of the divisor D, not just the generic point of X.
  • Believing the DT invariants of a log Calabi-Yau variety are always integers; for pairs with non-trivial log structure, the DT invariants can be rational due to the presence of strictly semistable objects supported on the divisor.
  • Confusing the scattering diagram in the Gross-Siebert program with the wall-crossing diagram in the space of stability conditions; the scattering diagram lives in the tropical base B0, while the wall-crossing diagram lives in Stab(X), and they are related by the mirror map.
  • Assuming the Fourier-Mukai transform for the Mukai flop is always an equivalence of the full derived categories; for non-primitive Mukai vectors, the moduli space may have singularities and the equivalence holds only for the derived categories of the smooth loci.

These advanced topics illustrate the deep interplay between stability conditions, geometric representation theory, and mirror symmetry across diverse geometric settings.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Stacks and Orbifolds

Let X be a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over C with projective coarse moduli space. The bounded derived category D^b(Coh(X)) carries a natural Bridgeland stability condition constructed by Abramovich and Polishchuk (2017) using the orbifold Chern character chorb and the orbifold Todd class tdorb. The central charge takes the form Z(E)=-∫X e-B-iω chorb(E) sqrt{tdorb(X)} where B+iω is a complexified Kähler class on the coarse space lifted to the stack. The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of μ-stable orbifold sheaves, defined by slope stability with respect to ω on the inertia stack. The space of stability conditions Stab(X) contains a component isomorphic to the universal cover of the complexified Kähler cone modulo the action of the orbifold autoequivalence group, which includes tensor products by line bundles from the inertia stack and spherical twists around structure sheaves of twisted sectors. Wall‑crossing in this component is governed by the orbifold Donaldson–Thomas invariants defined by Joyce and Song using the motivic Hall algebra of the stack. For a global quotient stack [X/G] with G finite, the stability condition descends from a G-equivariant stability condition on D^b(Coh(X)); the central charge integrates over the inertia components weighted by the age grading. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group N(X) equipped with the orbifold Euler pairing chiorb(E,F)=Σ_i(-1)^idimHom^i(E,F). When X is a root stack along a smooth divisor, the space of stability conditions fibers over the space of stability conditions on the base with fiber a product of copies of C^* corresponding to the discrete torsion parameters.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Representations of Algebras and the Happel–Reiten–Smale Tilt

Let A be a finite‑dimensional algebra of finite global dimension over an algebraically closed field. The bounded derived category D^b(mod-A) admits a canonical bounded t‑structure whose heart is mod-A. Given a torsion pair (T,F) in mod-A, the Happel–Reiten–Smale (HRS) tilt produces a new heart H=(F[1],T) which is the category of modules over the tilted algebra B=End_A(T) for a tilting module T. Bridgeland stability conditions on D^b(mod-A) can be constructed by lifting a King stability condition on mod-B via the derived equivalence D^b(mod-A)≃ D^b(mod-B). The central charge is Z(X)=-θ(dim H0H(X))+i θ(dim H-1H(X)) for a linear form θ on the Grothendieck group K0(A). The space of stability conditions Stab(A) is a complex manifold of dimension rank K0(A); its connected components correspond to different silting objects. For a gentle algebra, the space of stability conditions is homeomorphic to the complement of a hyperplane arrangement in C^n where the walls are given by the vanishing of the central charge on indecomposable objects. The support property is equivalent to the existence of a quadratic form Q on K0(A) negative definite on ker Z; such a form is provided by the Euler form chi(x,y)=Σ(-1)^idimExt^i(x,y). When A is the path algebra of an acyclic quiver, the space of stability conditions contains a component isomorphic to the universal cover of the space of stability conditions on the corresponding Calabi–Yau‑3 category via the Ginzburg dg‑algebra. The wall‑crossing formula for the motivic Hall algebra of mod-A reduces to the Kontsevich–Soibelman product of quantum dilogarithms associated to the spherical objects in the tilted heart.

Worked Example: Constructing a Stability Condition on a Tilted Heart
Let A=kQ be the path algebra of the Kronecker quiver 1rightrightarrows 2 over C. Consider the torsion pair in mod-A where T consists of representations with no direct summand isomorphic to the simple S1 at vertex 1, and F consists of representations generated by S1. Perform the HRS tilt to obtain the heart H. Describe a Bridgeland stability condition on D^b(mod-A) whose heart is H and compute the central charge on the indecomposable objects of H.
The tilted heart H is equivalent to mod-B where B is the endomorphism algebra of the tilting module T=S1⊕ P2 (with P2 the projective at vertex 2). The Grothendieck group K0(A)congZ2 has basis [S1],[S2]. In H, the simple objects are S1[1] and the cokernel of the map S1→ P2 (which is the regular representation of dimension vector (1,1)). Choose a stability parameter θ=(θ1,θ2) with θ1>0,θ2<0 and θ1+θ2=0. Define Z(X)=-θ(dim H0H(X))+i θ(dim H-1H(X)). For the simple S1[1], H0=0, H-1=S1 so Z=iθ1. For the regular object R, H0=R, H-1=0 so Z=-θ(dim R)=-θ1-θ2=0. To avoid zero central charge, perturb θ slightly so that θ1+θ2≠0. Then Z(R)=-(θ1+θ2)+i·0. The phase of S1[1] is π/2; the phase of R is π if θ1+θ2>0 or 0 if θ1+θ2<0. This gives a valid stability condition on H with the required heart.
Exam Strategy
When a question asks for a stability condition on a tilted heart, first identify the tilting object and the induced equivalence of derived categories. Write the central charge in terms of the stability parameter on the tilted algebra, then compute phases on the new simples. Remember that the support property is automatic for finite‑dimensional algebras because the Euler form provides the required quadratic form.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Toric Varieties and the GKZ Hypergeometric System

Let X_Σ be a smooth projective toric variety defined by a fan Σ in N_R. The bounded derived category D^b(Coh(X_Σ)) admits a full exceptional collection of line bundles O(D1),…,O(D_n) corresponding to a maximal chain of cones in the fan. The associated tilting object T=bigoplusO(D_i) yields a derived equivalence D^b(Coh(X_Σ))≃ D^b(mod-A) where A is the endomorphism algebra of T, a finite‑dimensional algebra presented by the quiver with relations coming from the toric data. Bridgeland stability conditions on D^b(Coh(X_Σ)) can be transported from King stability conditions on mod-A. The central charge is Z(E)=-∫X_Σ e-B-iωch(E)√(td(X_Σ)) with B+iω in the complexified Kähler cone. The space of stability conditions Stab(X_Σ) contains a component isomorphic to the universal cover of the complexified Kähler moduli space. The GKZ hypergeometric system associated to the fan Σ governs the periods of the mirror Landau–Ginzburg model; its solutions are the central charges of stability conditions on the mirror Fukaya category. Under homological mirror symmetry, the monodromy of the GKZ system around the large‑radius limit corresponds to the action of the spherical twist around the structure sheaf OX_Σ. The wall‑crossing of stability conditions on X_Σ is described by the scattering diagram of the Gross–Siebert program, which coincides with the wall‑crossing of the motivic Hall algebra of mod-A. For a toric Fano variety, the space of stability conditions is simply connected and the support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group equipped with the Euler pairing. The autoequivalence group acts by mutations of the exceptional collection, and the fundamental group of the stability manifold is the pure braid group on n strands.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Higgs Bundles

Let MDol(C,G) be the moduli space of semistable Higgs bundles of rank r and degree d on a smooth projective curve C of genus g≥2, with structure group a complex reductive group G. The derived category D^b(Coh(MDol)) carries a natural stability condition constructed by Bridgeland (2019) using the non‑abelian Hodge correspondence. The central charge is Z(E)=-∫MDol e-B-iωch(E)sqrt{td(MDol)} where ω is the hyperkähler Kähler form and B is the B‑field coming from the complex symplectic form. The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Hitchin fibration h:MDoltoA. The space of stability conditions Stab(MDol) contains a component fibered over the space of stability conditions on the base A with fiber the product of stability conditions on the derived categories of the fibers, which are abelian varieties. The wall‑crossing in this component is governed by the motivic Hall algebra of the category of Higgs bundles, and the Kontsevich–Soibelman wall‑crossing formula reproduces the wall‑crossing of the DT invariants of the associated 3‑dimensional Calabi–Yau category. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group equipped with the intersection pairing on the middle cohomology of MDol. For G=GL_r, the space of stability conditions is related to the space of stability conditions on the derived category of the character variety M_B(C,GL_r) via the P=W conjecture; the monodromy of the Hitchin system corresponds to the action of the mapping class group on the stability manifold.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Noncommutative Crepant Resolutions

Let R be a Gorenstein normal domain of dimension three with an isolated singularity, and let Λ=End_R(M) be a noncommutative crepant resolution (NCCR) in the sense of Van den Bergh, where M is a reflexive R-module that is a generator. The derived category D^b(mod-Λ) is equivalent to the derived category of coherent sheaves on a crepant resolution YtoSpec R when such a resolution exists. Bridgeland stability conditions on D^b(mod-Λ) can be constructed by pulling back a geometric stability condition on D^b(Coh(Y)) via the derived equivalence. The central charge is Z(E)=-∫_Y e-B-iωch(Φ(E))√(td(Y)) where Φ:D^b(mod-Λ)→ D^b(Coh(Y)) is the equivalence. The heart of the t‑structure is the category of perverse modules over Λ with respect to the resolution. The space of stability conditions Stab(Λ) contains a component isomorphic to the space of stability conditions on Y. The wall‑crossing of stability conditions on Λ corresponds to the flop transitions in the minimal model program for Y. The motivic Hall algebra of mod-Λ is isomorphic to the motivic Hall algebra of Coh(Y), and the integration map to the quantum torus sends the class of a simple Λ-module to the corresponding curve class in Y. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group N(Λ) equipped with the Euler form. For the conifold singularity xy=zw, the NCCR is given by the path algebra of the Klebanov–Witten quiver with superpotential; the space of stability conditions is a covering of C2 minus the discriminant locus, and the walls correspond to the vanishing of the central charge on the fractional branes.

  • Confusing the orbifold Chern character with the ordinary Chern character on the coarse space; the age shift in the inertia stack is essential for the correct central charge.
  • Assuming the HRS tilt always yields a heart equivalent to a module category; this holds only when the torsion pair comes from a tilting module, not for arbitrary torsion pairs.
  • Neglecting the role of the GKZ system in identifying the mirror map; the periods of the mirror Landau–Ginzburg model are solutions of the GKZ system, not arbitrary functions.
  • Treating the Hitchin fibration as a Lagrangian fibration in the sense of SYZ without the hyperkähler rotation; the perverse heart depends on the complex structure I not J.
  • Believing that every NCCR comes from a geometric crepant resolution; there exist NCCRs for singularities that admit no crepant resolution (e.g., certain quotient singularities in dimension three).
  • Confusing the motivic Hall algebra of the NCCR with the Hall algebra of the singularity; the equivalence of derived categories induces an isomorphism of Hall algebras only after passing to the motivic completion.
  • Assuming the space of stability conditions on a toric variety is always simply connected; for non‑Fano toric varieties the fundamental group can be non‑trivial due to the presence of non‑compact divisors.

Equivariant Bridgeland Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of G‑Equivariant Coherent Sheaves

Let G be a reductive algebraic group acting on a smooth projective variety X over the complex numbers. The G‑equivariant derived category D^b_G(Coh(X)) is the bounded derived category of G‑equivariant coherent sheaves. A Bridgeland stability condition on this triangulated category consists of a heart A of a bounded t‑structure and a group homomorphism Z: K0^G(X) → C, called the central charge, such that for every non‑zero object E in A the complex number Z(E) lies in the strict upper half‑plane, and the pair (A,Z) satisfies the support property with respect to a norm on the finite‑dimensional real vector space N^G(X) = K0^G(X) ⊗_Z R modulo the kernel of Z. The central charge is usually written as Z(E) = ∫_X e-B-iω ch^G(E) √(td^G(X)), where ch^G and td^G denote the equivariant Chern character and equivariant Todd class, B+iω is an equivariant Kähler class, and the integral is the equivariant push‑forward to a point, i.e. evaluation on the fundamental class in equivariant Chow homology. The space Stab_G(X) of such stability conditions carries a natural topology making it a complex manifold of dimension equal to rank N^G(X). The forgetful functor D^b_G(Coh(X)) → D^b(Coh(X)) induces a holomorphic map Stab_G(X) → Stab(X) which is a covering map onto its image; the deck transformation group is the subgroup of the equivariant Picard group acting trivially on the non‑equivariant numerical Grothendieck group. Wall‑crossing in Stab_G(X) is governed by the equivariant motivic Hall algebra of the heart A. The integration map sends the class of a G‑equivariant object to the corresponding element in the equivariant quantum torus, and the Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization holds in the completed equivariant quantum torus. Applications include the construction of stability conditions on GIT quotients X//G via the Kempf–Ness theorem, and the study of moduli spaces of G‑equivariant sheaves where the stability parameter varies in the equivariant Kähler cone.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Noncommutative Resolutions Beyond NCCRs

Let R be a normal Noetherian domain of dimension three with isolated singularities, and let Λ be a noncommutative algebra that is a resolution of singularities in the sense that the derived category D^b(mod‑Λ) is equivalent to the derived category of coherent sheaves on a resolution of singularities Y → Spec R, but Λ need not be a noncommutative crepant resolution (NCCR). Such algebras arise, for example, from partial resolutions or from non‑Gorenstein singularities where a crepant resolution does not exist. One can still construct Bridgeland stability conditions on D^b(mod‑Λ) by transporting a geometric stability condition on D^b(Coh(Y)) across the derived equivalence, provided Y exists. When no geometric resolution is available, a central charge can be defined directly on the numerical Grothendieck group N(Λ) = K0(mod‑Λ) ⊗_Z R using the Euler form χ(E,F) = Σ (-1)^i dim Ext^i(E,F). Choose a stability function Z: N(Λ) → C that factors through the Chern character map ch: N(Λ) → H^*(Y,Q) (if a resolution exists) or through a suitable trace map on the Hochschild homology of Λ. The heart of the associated t‑structure is obtained by iterated tilting with respect to torsion pairs defined by the slope function μ_Z(E) = -Re Z(E)/Im Z(E). The space Stab(Λ) of stability conditions contains a distinguished component that maps isomorphically onto the space of stability conditions on any geometric resolution Y when such a resolution exists. Wall‑crossing in this component is described by mutations of the algebra Λ; each wall corresponds to a change of the heart induced by a tilting mutation, and the motivic Hall algebra of mod‑Λ is isomorphic to the motivic Hall algebra of Coh(Y) after motivic completion. The integration map to the quantum torus sends the class of a simple Λ‑module to the curve class it represents in Y, and the Kontsevich–Soibelman wall‑crossing formula reproduces the flop transitions in the minimal model program for Y. The support property holds with respect to the Euler form on N(Λ), and the numerical Grothendieck group carries a natural lattice structure coming from the classes of projective Λ‑modules.

Examiner's trap
A common error is to treat the equivariant central charge of a skyscraper sheaf at a fixed point as the ordinary integral of its Chern character. Explain why the equivariant central charge must be evaluated in the equivariant Chow group and how the fixed‑point basis enters the computation.
The equivariant central charge Z^G(E) = ∫_X e-B-iω ch^G(E) √(td^G(X)) takes values in the equivariant Chow group A^*_G(pt) ⊗ C, which is isomorphic to the polynomial ring C[𝔱] where 𝔱 is the Lie algebra of the maximal torus of G. For a skyscraper sheaf O_x at a fixed point x, the equivariant Chern character ch^G(O_x) is the class of the fixed point in equivariant Chow, not the ordinary fundamental class. The integral ∫_X is the equivariant push‑forward to a point, which evaluates the product against the equivariant fundamental class of X. In the fixed‑point basis, this push‑forward becomes a sum over fixed points of the localisation formula: Z^G(O_x) = Σp∈X^G (e-B-iω ch^G(O_x) √(td^G(X)))_p / e_G(N_p X), where e_G(N_p X) is the equivariant Euler class of the normal bundle at p. The ordinary integral would ignore the denominator e_G(N_p X) and the dependence on the torus weights, leading to an incorrect central charge that does not satisfy the support property in the equivariant numerical Grothendieck group.
Exam‑day strategy
When a problem asks for the central charge in an equivariant setting, first write down the equivariant Chern character in the basis of fixed‑point contributions, then pair with the equivariant Kähler class using the localisation formula. Keep track of the torus weights in the denominator; they are essential for the support property.

Wall‑Crossing for Stability Conditions on Triangulated Categories with Non‑Finite Hearts

The classical Kontsevich–Soibelman wall‑crossing formula assumes that the heart of the t‑structure is a finite length abelian category, so that the Hall algebra is graded by a finite‑rank lattice and the product of wall‑crossing factors is a finite product in the quantum torus. In many geometric situations — for instance, the category of perverse coherent sheaves on a non‑compact Calabi–Yau threefold, or the heart obtained by tilting with respect to a stability condition whose central charge takes values in a non‑discrete subgroup of C — the heart is not of finite length. The Joyce–Song theory of generalized Donaldson–Thomas invariants extends the wall‑crossing formalism to this setting by working in the motivic Hall algebra completed with respect to the filtration by the support property. One defines a stability function Z on the numerical Grothendieck group N(D) and a notion of semistability for objects in the heart A. The stack of objects Obj(A) is stratified by Harder–Narasimhan type, and the integration map ∫: H^mot(Obj(A)) → QTor(N(D)) sends the class of a semistable object to its quantum torus element. The wall‑crossing formula then takes the form of an identity in the completed quantum torus: the product over rays ℓ in the central charge plane of the symplectomorphisms Φ_ℓ = exp( Σγ∈ℓ∩Γ Ω(γ) e_γ ) is independent of the stability condition, where Ω(γ) are the generalized DT invariants defined via the motivic weight. The convergence of the infinite product is guaranteed by a strengthened support property, often called the local support property, which requires that for every compact subset K of the central charge plane there exists a constant C_K such that ||γ|| ≤ C_K |Z(γ)| for all γ with Z(γ) ∈ K. This condition controls the growth of the invariants and ensures that the factorization makes sense in the completion. Applications include the wall‑crossing of stability conditions on the derived category of coherent sheaves on a local Calabi–Yau threefold without compact divisor, and the variation of stability conditions on the Fukaya category of a non‑compact symplectic manifold.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps and the Quantum Cohomology Ring

Let X be a smooth projective variety and let Mg,n(X,β) denote the moduli stack of stable maps of genus g with n marked points representing the curve class β ∈ H2(X,Z). The derived category D^b(Coh(Mg,n(X,β))) carries a natural family of Bridgeland stability conditions constructed from the Gromov–Witten theory of X. The central charge is defined by Z(E) = ∫[Mg,n(X,β)]vir e-B-iω ch(E) √(td(Mg,n(X,β))) where the integral is taken against the virtual fundamental class. The Kähler class B+iω lives in the quantum cohomology ring QH^*(X) = H^*(X) ⊗ Λ, with Λ the Novikov ring, and the central charge takes values in Λ. The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the evaluation morphisms ev_i: Mg,n(X,β) → X. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mg,n(X,β)) contains a component that maps to the space of stability conditions on the Fukaya category Fuk(X) under the homological mirror symmetry equivalence D^b(Coh(Mg,n(X,β))) ≃ Fuk(X). Wall‑crossing in this component corresponds to the change of stability conditions in the quantum cohomology ring as the Kähler parameter crosses walls in the extended Kähler cone. The Donaldson–Thomas invariants of the moduli space of stable maps, defined via the motivic Hall algebra of the heart, compute the Gromov–Witten invariants of X through the DT/GW correspondence. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group equipped with the Euler pairing twisted by the virtual class, and the numerical group is naturally identified with the quantum cohomology lattice.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Matrix Factorizations for Non‑Isolated Singularities and the Orlov Equivalence

Consider a Landau–Ginzburg model (X,W) where X is a smooth quasi‑projective variety and W: X → A1 is a regular function whose critical locus Crit(W) is not necessarily isolated. The derived category of matrix factorizations MF(X,W) is equivalent, by Orlov's theorem, to the singularity category Dsg(Crit(W)) = D^b(Coh(Crit(W))) / Perf(Crit(W)). When Crit(W) has positive dimension, the category MF(X,W) is a Calabi–Yau category of fractional dimension. Bridgeland stability conditions on MF(X,W) can be constructed using the central charge Z(E) = ∫γ Ω_E, where Ω_E is the period integral of the holomorphic volume form on the Milnor fiber of W along a relative cycle γ ∈ Hmid(W-1(t), W-1(t)∩Crit(W); Z). The periods satisfy the Picard–Fuchs equations associated to the Gauss–Manin connection, and the central charge takes values in the space of solutions of this differential system. The heart of the t‑structure is the category of graded matrix factorizations with respect to a chosen grading on the singularity. The space of stability conditions Stab(MF(X,W)) is a covering of the complement of the discriminant locus in the space of marginal deformations of W. Wall‑crossing corresponds to the variation of mixed Hodge structure on the vanishing cohomology of W, and the Kontsevich–Soibelman formula reproduces the monodromy of the Gauss–Manin connection. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group N(MF) equipped with the Euler form χ(E,F) = Σ (-1)^i dim HomMF(E,F[i]). The Orlov equivalence identifies N(MF) with the numerical Grothendieck group of the singularity category, and under this identification the space of stability conditions on MF(X,W) maps to the space of stability conditions on a resolution of Crit(W) when such a resolution exists. This provides a bridge between the wall‑crossing of matrix factorizations and the flop transitions in the minimal model program for the resolution.

  • Confusing the equivariant central charge with the ordinary central charge; the equivariant version lives in the equivariant Chow group and requires localisation at fixed points.
  • Assuming every noncommutative resolution is an NCCR; many algebras give resolutions that are not crepant and lack a Calabi–Yau property.
  • Applying the finite‑length wall‑crossing formula to hearts that are not of finite length without completing the Hall algebra.
  • Neglecting the virtual fundamental class when defining the central charge on moduli spaces of stable maps; the ordinary fundamental class does not exist in the expected dimension.
  • Treating the period integrals for non‑isolated singularities as ordinary integrals on the Milnor fiber; they are relative cycles in the vanishing cohomology.
  • Overlooking the local support property when the numerical Grothendieck group is not discrete in the central charge plane.
  • Identifying the quantum cohomology ring with the ordinary cohomology ring in the DT/GW correspondence; the Novikov variables are essential for convergence.

The advanced sections above illustrate how stability conditions adapt to equivariant, noncommutative, non‑finite, enumerative, and singular settings while preserving the core formalism of central charges, hearts, and wall‑crossing.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Parabolic Higgs Bundles

Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g ≥ 2 equipped with a divisor D of marked points. A parabolic Higgs bundle on (X,D) consists of a vector bundle E together with a Higgs field φ : E → E ⊗ ΩX(D) and a weighted flag at each point of D preserved by the residue of φ. The moduli space Mpar(X,D) of semistable parabolic Higgs bundles of fixed rank and parabolic degree is a quasi‑projective hyperkähler variety. Its derived category Db(Coh(Mpar)) carries a natural family of Bridgeland stability conditions constructed by combining the Hitchin fibration with the Fourier–Mukai transform associated to the universal parabolic Higgs bundle. The central charge is defined by integrating the holomorphic symplectic form against the Chern character twisted by the parabolic weights, yielding a map Z : Knum(Mpar) → ℂ that respects the support property with respect to the natural polarization coming from the determinant line bundle on the moduli space. Wall‑crossing in this setting is governed by the Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization applied to the motivic Hall algebra of the heart of perverse coherent sheaves on the Hitchin base. The resulting wall‑crossing formula reproduces the parabolic version of the non‑abelian Hodge correspondence, identifying the Donaldson–Thomas invariants of Mpar with the mixed Hodge numbers of the corresponding character variety. Recent work of Bussi–Joyce–Meinhardt extends the integration map to the motivic Hall algebra of the parabolic heart, proving that the generalized DT invariants satisfy the expected integrality and symmetry properties.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Flat Connections and the Nonabelian Hodge Correspondence

For a smooth projective curve X of genus g ≥ 2, the moduli space MB(X) of semisimple flat GLn(ℂ)‑connections (the Betti moduli space) is an affine algebraic variety with a natural holomorphic symplectic structure. The nonabelian Hodge theorem provides a diffeomorphism MB(X) ≃ MDol(X) between the Betti space and the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs bundles. Transporting the complex structure of MDol yields a hyperkähler rotation that identifies the derived category Db(Coh(MB)) with the Fukaya category of MDol under homological mirror symmetry. Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(MB)) are constructed by pulling back the stability conditions on the Hitchin system via the Hitchin fibration h : MDol → A, where A is the Hitchin base. The central charge takes the form Z(E) = ∫γ e−B−iω ch(E) for a suitable complexified Kähler class B+iω on MB. The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Lagrangian fibration h. Wall‑crossing as the Kähler parameter varies corresponds to the change of stability conditions on the Hitchin system and is encoded by the Kontsevich–Soibelman wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the heart. The Donaldson–Thomas invariants of MB defined via this Hall algebra compute the BPS invariants of the associated N=2 supersymmetric gauge theory, and the integration map of Joyce–Song identifies them with the cohomological Hall algebra of the quiver with potential arising from the Higgs branch. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group equipped with the Euler pairing twisted by the symplectic form, and the space of stability conditions Stab(MB) contains a connected component isomorphic to the universal cover of the complement of the discriminant locus in the Hitchin base.

Worked Example: Central Charge on the Betti Moduli Space
Let X be a genus‑2 curve and consider the moduli space MB of rank‑2 flat connections with fixed determinant. Suppose a class α ∈ Knum(MB) has Chern character ch(α) = (2, 0, −1) in the basis (rank, c1, ch2). Take a complexified Kähler class B+iω with B = 0 and ω the standard symplectic form normalized so that ∫MB ω2 = 1. Compute the central charge Z(α) = ∫MB e−iω ch(α).
Expand e−iω = 1 − iω − ω2/2. Pair with ch(α) = 2 − 0·ω − 1·ω2. The integral picks the degree‑4 component: ∫ (2)(−ω2/2) + (−1)(1) = −∫ ω2 − 1 = −1 − 1 = −2. Hence Z(α) = −2.
Exam‑Day Strategy
When a question asks for the central charge on a hyperkähler moduli space, first identify the complexified Kähler class and the Chern character in the numerical Grothendieck group. Expand the exponential only up to the top degree of the variety; lower‑degree terms integrate to zero. Remember that the symplectic form is normalized by the Beauville–Bogomolov form, so its top self‑intersection is a known constant (often 1). This reduces the computation to a simple polynomial evaluation.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Calabi–Yau Fourfolds and the Generalized DT/PT Correspondence

Let Y be a smooth projective Calabi–Yau fourfold with trivial canonical bundle. The derived category Db(Coh(Y)) admits a Serre functor of shift 4, making it a 4‑Calabi–Yau category. Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(Y)) are constructed by adapting the Bayer–Macrì–Toda method: one first defines a weak stability condition using a pair of divisor classes (B, ω) with ω ample, then proves the support property by bounding the mass of semistable objects via the Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality for torsion‑free sheaves on fourfolds. The central charge is ZB,ω(E) = ∫Y e−B−iω ch(E) √td(Y), where the Todd class correction ensures compatibility with the Mukai pairing. The heart of the associated t‑structure is obtained by a double tilt of Coh(Y) along the walls determined by the discriminant Δ(E) = 2r ch2 − (r−1)c12. Wall‑crossing in this setting is governed by the Joyce–Song generalized DT invariants, which are defined using the motivic Hall algebra of the heart and satisfy the wall‑crossing formula of Kontsevich–Soibelman. The DT/PT correspondence for fourfolds relates the Donaldson–Thomas invariants of ideal sheaves of curves to the Pandharipande–Thomas stable pair invariants; the correspondence is proved by comparing the wall‑crossing formulas on the two sides of the wall where the central charge aligns the phases of the structure sheaf and the ideal sheaf. Recent results of Cao–Maulik–Toda establish the correspondence for local Calabi–Yau fourfolds by using the vertex formalism and the topological vertex. The space of stability conditions Stab(Y) contains a distinguished component that maps to the complexified Kähler cone via the central charge map, and the global structure of this component is conjectured to be described by the autoequivalence group generated by spherical twists and the Fourier–Mukai transform associated to the universal sheaf on the moduli space of stable sheaves.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Derived Stacks and the Derived Moduli of Objects

Let 𝔛 be a derived Artin stack locally of finite presentation over ℂ, for instance the derived moduli stack of objects in a Calabi–Yau category 𝒞. The derived category of quasi‑coherent sheaves Dqc(𝔛) carries a natural symmetric monoidal structure and a Serre functor when 𝔛 is proper and has a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of Pantev–Toën–Vaquié–Vezzosi. Bridgeland stability conditions on Dqc(𝔛) are defined by requiring the heart to be a derived abelian category in the sense of Porta–Yu, and the central charge to factor through the numerical Grothendieck group Knum(𝔛) equipped with the Euler pairing induced by the shifted symplectic form. The construction uses the derived Hall algebra of 𝔛, defined by Joyce via the ∞‑category of correspondences in the ∞‑topos of derived stacks. The integration map from the motivic Hall algebra to the quantum torus is replaced by a map to the derived quantum torus, where the commutation relations are governed by the derived Euler form. Wall‑crossing is encoded by the derived Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization, which lives in the completed derived Hall algebra and reproduces the monodromy of the Gauss–Manin connection on the cohomology of the derived moduli stack. The support property is formulated using the local support property of Joyce, which requires the central charge to be proper on the set of semistable objects of fixed numerical class. When 𝔛 is the derived moduli stack of sheaves on a Calabi–Yau threefold, the space of stability conditions Stab(𝔛) recovers the classical space Stab(Db(Coh(X))) and the derived wall‑crossing formula specializes to the Joyce–Song formula for generalized DT invariants. This framework also accommodates stability conditions on categories of matrix factorizations for non‑isolated singularities, where the derived stack is the critical locus of a Landau–Ginzburg potential.

  • Confusing the parabolic weights with ordinary Chern characters; the central charge must incorporate the weights as shifts in the grading.
  • Assuming the Hitchin fibration is proper on the whole moduli space; it is only proper on the nilpotent cone, and wall‑crossing formulas require compactly supported cohomology.
  • Neglecting the Todd class correction in the central charge for Calabi–Yau fourfolds; without √td(Y) the Mukai pairing is not preserved.
  • Treating the derived Hall algebra as an ordinary algebra; its multiplication is homotopy‑coherent and the wall‑crossing formula lives in a completed ∞‑algebra.
  • Overlooking the local support property when the numerical Grothendieck group is not discrete; the central charge must be proper on each numerical class separately.
  • Identifying the DT/PT correspondence for fourfolds with the threefold case; the vertex formalism and the topological vertex are essential new ingredients.
  • Assuming every derived stack admits a global stability condition; existence often requires a quasi‑projective atlas and a suitable ample line bundle.

These advanced topics illustrate how Bridgeland stability extends to parabolic Higgs bundles, flat connections, higher‑dimensional Calabi–Yau varieties, and derived moduli stacks while preserving the core formalism of central charges, hearts, and wall‑crossing.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Vector Bundles on Curves and the Verlinde Formula

Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g ≥ 2 over ℂ, and let MC(r, d) denote the moduli space of S-equivalence classes of semistable vector bundles of rank r and degree d on C. When gcd(r, d) = 1, this space is a smooth projective variety of dimension r2(g−1)+1, and its Picard group is generated by the determinant line bundle ℒ = det Rπ*(ℰ ⊗ πC*ωC1/2), where ℰ is a universal bundle (or a twisted universal bundle when no universal bundle exists). The Verlinde formula computes the dimension of the space of conformal blocks H0(MC(r, d), ℒ⊗k) for a positive integer k (the level) as a sum over dominant weights of the affine Lie algebra ŝl(r) at level k.

Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(MC(r, d))) provide a categorical framework for understanding the Verlinde formula. The heart of a stability condition can be taken as the category of coherent sheaves, and the central charge is defined via the Chern character and the Todd class: Z(E) = −∫M ch(E) · e−iπω · td(M)1/2, where ω is an ample class proportional to c1(ℒ). The space of stability conditions Stab(MC(r, d)) contains a component mapping to the complexified Kähler cone, and wall-crossing in this component corresponds to changes in the Verlinde numbers as the level k varies or as the curve C degenerates.

The connection to the Verlinde formula is mediated by the quantum cohomology of MC(r, d). The small quantum cohomology ring QH*(M) is isomorphic to the fusion ring of the Wess-Zumino-Witten model at level k, and the Verlinde numbers are the structure constants of this ring. Stability conditions on Db(Coh(M)) categorify this isomorphism: the derived category carries an action of the braid group via spherical twists, and the monodromy of the Gauss-Manin connection on the quantum cohomology matches the wall-crossing autoequivalences. In particular, the quantum differential equation (the Dubrovin connection) on QH*(M) is equivalent to the KZ connection on the space of conformal blocks, and the Stokes data of this connection are governed by the Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing formula in the Hall algebra of Db(Coh(M)).

When C degenerates to a nodal curve, the moduli space MC(r, d) acquires a stratification by the type of the vector bundle at the node. The Verlinde formula for the nodal curve is given by the factorization rule of conformal field theory, which states that the space of conformal blocks on the nodal curve is the direct sum over intermediate weights of the tensor product of conformal blocks on the normalization. Categorically, this corresponds to a semi-orthogonal decomposition of Db(Coh(MC(r, d))) induced by a stability condition whose heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the stratification. The wall-crossing formula for this degeneration is the categorical Verlinde formula, proved by Teleman using the loop group action on the affine Grassmannian and the geometric Satake equivalence.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Higgs Bundles and the Hitchin Integrable System

Let MHiggs(C, G) be the moduli space of semistable Higgs bundles (E, φ) on a smooth projective curve C of genus g ≥ 2, where G is a complex reductive group. This space is a non-compact hyperkähler manifold of dimension 2(g−1) dim G, equipped with the Hitchin fibration h: MHiggs → B = ⊕i=1rank G H0(C, KCdi), where di are the degrees of the fundamental invariants of G. The generic fiber of h is an abelian variety (a Prym variety of the spectral curve), and the fibration is completely integrable in the sense of Liouville-Arnold.

Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(MHiggs)) are constructed using the perverse heart with respect to the Hitchin fibration. The central charge is defined by Z(E) = ∫M ch(E) · e−iπω · td(M)1/2, where ω is a Kähler class pulled back from the base B plus a multiple of the relative ample class on the fibers. The support property holds because the Hitchin fibration is proper on the nilpotent cone h−1(0), and the central charge is proper on the set of semistable objects of fixed numerical class. The space of stability conditions Stab(MHiggs) contains a distinguished component that maps to the complexified Kähler cone of MHiggs, and its global structure is governed by the wall-crossing of perverse coherent sheaves as the Kähler class crosses walls where the phases of skyscraper sheaves on fibers align with those of structure sheaves of Lagrangian subvarieties.

The wall-crossing formula in this setting is intimately related to the BPS invariants of the Hitchin system. The cohomological Hall algebra of the category of Higgs bundles (or equivalently, the category of coherent sheaves on the Hitchin base with support on the discriminant locus) carries an action of the BPS Lie algebra, whose generators correspond to the vanishing cycles of the Hitchin fibration. The Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in this Hall algebra reproduces the monodromy of the Gauss-Manin connection on the cohomology of the smooth fibers, which is the Hitchin connection on the space of conformal blocks. This provides a categorical interpretation of the non-abelian Hodge correspondence: the derived category Db(Coh(MHiggs)) is equivalent to the derived category of constructible sheaves on the character variety MBetti(C, G) via the Hitchin fibration and the Fourier-Mukai transform on the generic fibers, and stability conditions on the two sides correspond under this equivalence.

For G = GL(n), the moduli space MHiggs admits a mirror symmetry with the moduli space of Higgs bundles for the Langlands dual group G∨ = GL(n) (self-dual). The SYZ conjecture predicts that the Hitchin fibration is a special Lagrangian torus fibration, and mirror symmetry exchanges the A-model of MHiggs with the B-model of MHiggs∨. Bridgeland stability conditions provide the categorical framework for this mirror symmetry: the Fukaya category of MHiggs (with its Lagrangian sections and fibers) is equivalent to Db(Coh(MHiggs∨)), and stability conditions on the Fukaya category correspond to stability conditions on the derived category of coherent sheaves. The wall-crossing of stability conditions on the Fukaya category is governed by the Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing formula for the BPS invariants of the Hitchin system, which are the refined BPS invariants of the associated N=2 supersymmetric gauge theory.

Worked Example: Wall-Crossing for Rank 2 Higgs Bundles on a Genus 2 Curve
Let C be a genus 2 curve, and consider the moduli space M = MHiggs(C, SL(2)) of rank 2 Higgs bundles with trivial determinant. The Hitchin base is B = H0(C, KC2) ≅ ℂ3. The discriminant locus Δ ⊂ B parametrizes spectral curves with nodes. Describe the wall-crossing of Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(M)) as the Kähler class ω crosses a wall where the phase of 𝒪F (structure sheaf of a generic fiber) aligns with the phase of 𝒪p (skyscraper sheaf at a point p ∈ M).
Solution. The numerical Grothendieck group Knum(M) is generated by the classes of 𝒪F and 𝒪p. The central charge is Z(E) = −∫M ch(E) · e−iπω · td(M)1/2. For a generic fiber F (an abelian surface), ch(𝒪F) = [F] and ∫F td(F)1/2 = 1. For a point p, ch(𝒪p) = [p] and ∫p td(p)1/2 = 1. Let ω = tωB + ωrel, where ωB is pulled back from B and ωrel is relatively ample. Then Z(𝒪F) = −∫F e−iπωrel · td(F)1/2 = −e−iπ∫Fωrel (since ωB restricts to 0 on F). And Z(𝒪p) = −e−iπ(t∫pωB + ∫pωrel) = −e−iπ∫pωrel (since ωB is pulled back from B and p maps to a point in B). The phases align when arg Z(𝒪F) = arg Z(𝒪p) mod 2π, i.e., when ∫F ωrel ≡ ∫p ωrel mod 2. This defines a real codimension-1 wall in the Kähler cone. Crossing this wall, the heart of the stability condition tilts: on one side, the heart is Coh(M); on the other side, it is the category of perverse coherent sheaves 0Per(M/B) with respect to the Hitchin fibration. The wall-crossing formula in the Hall algebra is Φ𝒪p ∘ Φ𝒪F = Φ𝒪F ∘ Φ𝒪p, where ΦE is the spherical twist associated to the spherical object E. This identity reflects the fact that the monodromy of the Hitchin connection around the discriminant locus is trivial on the cohomology of the generic fiber.
Exam Strategy: Identifying the Heart in Hitchin Systems
When a question asks about stability conditions on moduli spaces of Higgs bundles, the heart is almost always the perverse heart relative to the Hitchin fibration, not the standard Coh heart. Check whether the central charge uses a Kähler class with a component pulled back from the base B — this is the hallmark of the perverse construction. The wall-crossing walls correspond to alignments of phases of objects supported on fibers versus objects supported on sections (or the zero section). The BPS Lie algebra generators are the vanishing cycles of the fibration, and their commutation relations give the wall-crossing formula. Memorize the sequence: Hitchin fibration → perverse heart → vanishing cycles → BPS Lie algebra → KS factorization → monodromy of Hitchin connection.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of G-Bundles and the Geometric Satake Equivalence

Let G be a complex reductive group, and let BunG(C) be the moduli stack of G-bundles on a smooth projective curve C. The derived category Db(Coh(BunG)) carries a natural action of the loop group G((t)) via Hecke correspondences. The geometric Satake equivalence identifies the category of representations of the Langlands dual group G∨ with the category of G[[t]]-equivariant perverse sheaves on the affine Grassmannian GrG = G((t))/G[[t]]. This equivalence is monoidal, with convolution of perverse sheaves corresponding to tensor product of representations.

Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(BunG)) are constructed using the stratification by Harder-Narasimhan type. The stack BunG admits a stratification indexed by dominant coweights of G, where the stratum BunGλ parametrizes G-bundles whose Harder-Narasimhan polygon has slope λ. The heart of the stability condition is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to this stratification, and the central charge is defined by integrating the Chern character against a stability parameter in the complexified Kähler cone of the wonderful compactification of BunG. The support property holds because the stratification is finite and the central charge is proper on each stratum.

The space of stability conditions Stab(BunG) is closely related to the quantum Langlands correspondence. The quantum geometric Langlands conjecture predicts an equivalence between Db(Coh(BunG)) and the derived category of D-modules on BunG∨ twisted by a parameter ψ. Under this equivalence, stability conditions on the coherent side correspond to opers on the D-module side. The wall-crossing of stability conditions on Db(Coh(BunG)) corresponds to the monodromy of the quantum connection on the space of opers, which is governed by the quantum Weyl group action. The Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing formula in the Hall algebra of BunG reproduces the braid group relations of the quantum Weyl group.

For G = GL(n), the moduli stack BunGL(n) is the stack of rank n vector bundles. The derived category Db(Coh(BunGL(n))) is equivalent to the category of factorization modules over the Chiral algebra of the W-algebra associated to ŝl(n). Stability conditions on this category are classified by opers for ŝl(n) on the curve C, and the wall-crossing formula is the fusion rule of the W-algebra. The Verlinde formula for the dimension of the space of conformal blocks appears as the Euler characteristic of the moduli space of stable bundles with respect to a stability condition whose central charge is the quantum determinant of the oper.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Parabolic Bundles and the Mehta-Seshadri Correspondence

Let C be a smooth projective curve with marked points p1, …, pn, and let α = (α1, …, αn) be a collection of parabolic weights, where each αi is a sequence of rational numbers 0 ≤ αi,1 < … < αi,r < 1. A parabolic bundle on (C, p1, …, pn) is a vector bundle E with a flag of subspaces Epi = Fi,1 ⊃ Fi,2 ⊃ … ⊃ Fi,r ⊃ 0 at each marked point. The parabolic degree is degpar(E) = deg(E) + Σi,j αi,j dim(Fi,j/Fi,j+1), and the parabolic slope is μpar(E) = degpar(E)/rank(E). A parabolic bundle is parabolic stable if every proper parabolic subbundle has strictly smaller parabolic slope.

The moduli space Mpar(C, α) of parabolic stable bundles of fixed rank and parabolic degree is a smooth projective variety when the weights are generic. The Mehta-Seshadri correspondence identifies this moduli space with the moduli space of unitary representations of the fundamental group of the punctured curve π1(C {p1, …, pn}) with prescribed conjugacy classes at the punctures determined by the weights α. This is a parabolic version of the Narasimhan-Seshadri theorem.

Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(Mpar(C, α))) are constructed by pulling back the stability conditions from the moduli space of vector bundles on the logarithmic curve (C, D) where D = Σ pi. The central charge incorporates the parabolic weights as shifts in the grading: Z(E) = −∫M chpar(E) · e−iπω · td(M)1/2, where chpar is the parabolic Chern character defined using the logarithmic tangent bundle. The heart is the category of coherent sheaves, and the support property holds because the parabolic weights are generic.

Wall-crossing in Stab(Mpar) occurs when the parabolic weights cross walls where the parabolic slope of a subbundle equals the parabolic slope of the whole bundle. These walls are exactly the walls of the parabolic chamber structure on the weight space. The wall-crossing formula is governed by the Hall algebra of parabolic sheaves, which is a module over the Hall algebra of ordinary sheaves on C. The Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in this Hall algebra reproduces the fusion rules of the modular tensor category associated to the quantum group at a root of unity, which categorifies the Verlinde formula for parabolic bundles. The quantum Langlands correspondence for parabolic bundles relates Db(Coh(Mpar)) to the category of D-modules on the moduli space of parabolic local systems, and stability conditions correspond to parabolic opers.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Local Systems and the Geometric Langlands Correspondence

Let MBetti(C, G) be the character variety (moduli space of G-local systems) on a smooth projective curve C of genus g ≥ 2. This is an affine algebraic variety of dimension (2g−2) dim G + 2 dim Z(G), singular at the reducible representations. The geometric Langlands correspondence predicts an equivalence between the derived category of D-modules on BunG(C) and the derived category of coherent sheaves on MBetti(C, G∨), where G∨ is the Langlands dual group.

Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(Coh(MBetti(C, G))) are constructed using the non-abelian Hodge correspondence, which identifies MBetti with the moduli space of Higgs bundles MHiggs as a real analytic space (but not as a complex algebraic variety). The stability conditions on MBetti are pulled back from MHiggs via this correspondence. The central charge is defined using the Hitchin base and the period map: Z(E) = ∫M ch(E) · e−iπω · td(M)1/2, where ω is a Kähler class on MHiggs pulled back to MBetti. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Hitchin fibration on MHiggs.

The space of stability conditions Stab(MBetti) is acted upon by the mapping class group of C, which corresponds to the braid group action on Db(Coh(MHiggs)) via spherical twists. The wall-crossing formula is the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the Hall algebra of MHiggs, which matches the monodromy of the Gauss-Manin connection on the cohomology of the Hitchin fibers. This monodromy is the Hitchin connection on the space of conformal blocks, and its categorical lift is the braid group action on the derived category.

The quantum geometric Langlands conjecture at parameter ψ = 0 (the classical limit) states that Db(Coh(MBetti(C, G∨))) is equivalent to the category of D-modules on BunG(C). Under this equivalence, stability conditions on the coherent side correspond to opers for G∨ on C. The quantum Langlands correspondence at generic ψ deforms this equivalence, and stability conditions on the deformed category correspond to quantum opers. The wall-crossing of stability conditions corresponds to the quantum Weyl group action on the space of quantum opers, which is governed by the quantum KZ equations.

  • Confusing the parabolic weights with ordinary Chern characters; the central charge must incorporate the weights as shifts in the grading via the parabolic Chern character.
  • Assuming the Hitchin fibration is proper on the whole moduli space; it is only proper on the nilpotent cone, and wall-crossing formulas require compactly supported cohomology or the perverse heart.
  • Neglecting the Todd class correction in the central charge for moduli spaces of higher-dimensional varieties; without √td(M) the Mukai pairing is not preserved and the support property fails.
  • Treating the Hall algebra of a stack as an ordinary algebra; its multiplication is homotopy-coherent and the wall-crossing formula lives in a completed ∞-algebra.
  • Overlooking the local support property when the numerical Grothendieck group is not discrete; the central charge must be proper on each numerical class separately, not just globally.
  • Identifying the DT/PT correspondence for moduli spaces of bundles on curves with the threefold case; the wall-crossing is governed by the Verlinde formula and the fusion rules of the WZW model, not by the topological vertex.
  • Assuming every moduli stack admits a global stability condition; existence often requires a quasi-projective coarse moduli space and a suitable ample line bundle, which may not exist for non-reductive groups or non-generic weights.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Instantons and the ADHM Construction

The moduli space of framed instantons on ℝ⁴, or equivalently on ℙ² with framing at infinity, is constructed via the ADHM (Atiyah-Drinfeld-Hitchin-Manin) description as a hyperkähler quotient. For gauge group U(r) and instanton number k, the ADHM data consist of complex vector spaces V ≅ ℂᵏ, W ≅ ℂʳ and linear maps B₁, B₂ ∈ End(V), I ∈ Hom(W, V), J ∈ Hom(V, W) satisfying the ADHM equations [B₁, B₂] + IJ = 0 and the stability condition that no proper subspace of V is invariant under B₁, B₂ and contains Im(I). The moduli space M(r, k) is a smooth quasi-projective variety of dimension 4rk. Bridgeland stability conditions on Dᵇ(Coh(M(r, k))) are constructed using the Nakajima quiver variety structure: M(r, k) is the moduli space of representations of the framed Jordan quiver with dimension vector (k, r). The central charge is defined via the equivariant Chern character with respect to the torus action T = (ℂ*)² × (ℂ*)ʳ scaling the ℝ⁴ coordinates and the framing. For an object E ∈ Dᵇ(Coh(M(r, k))), Z(E) = ∫M(r, k) chT(E) · e-iπ ω · tdT(M(r, k))1/2, where ω is an equivariant Kähler class. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Hilbert-Chow morphism M(r, k) → Symᵏ(ℂ²) × ℙr-1. The space of stability conditions Stab(M(r, k)) contains a distinguished component isomorphic to the universal cover of the space of stability parameters for the quiver, which is ℂr+1 minus a hyperplane arrangement. Wall-crossing in this space corresponds to the variation of the ADHM stability parameter ζ ∈ ℝ, and the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization reproduces the Nakajima quiver variety wall-crossing formula for the BPS invariants of the quiver. The DT invariants of M(r, k) are identified with the equivariant Donaldson invariants of ℙ² via the Maulik-Okounkov correspondence, and the wall-crossing formula matches the blow-up formula for Donaldson invariants. The motivic Hall algebra of M(r, k) is isomorphic to the spherical Hall algebra of the Jordan quiver, and the integration map to the quantum torus recovers the Nekrasov partition function. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group Knum(M(r, k)) ⊗ ℚ, which is generated by the classes of the tautological bundles associated to the universal instanton bundle.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Vortices and the Bradlow Limit

The moduli space of vortices on a compact Riemann surface C of genus g ≥ 2, with gauge group U(r) and vortex number d, is a Kähler manifold Vr,d(C) of complex dimension 2rd + r²(g-1). It parametrizes pairs (A, φ) where A is a unitary connection on a Hermitian vector bundle E of rank r and degree d, and φ ∈ Ω⁰(C, E) is a section satisfying the vortex equations F_A + i(φφ* - τ·Id) = 0, ∂̄_A φ = 0, for a real parameter τ > 0. As τ → ∞, the Bradlow limit identifies Vr,d(C) with the symmetric product Symᵈ(C) × Jacd(C) when r = 1, and for r > 1 with a projective bundle over the moduli space of stable bundles Mr,d(C). Bridgeland stability conditions on Dᵇ(Coh(Vr,d(C))) are constructed using the symplectic vortex equations and the Hamiltonian reduction picture. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫Vr,d ch(E) · e-iπ ω_τ · td(Vr,d)1/2, where ω_τ is the Kähler form depending on τ. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Bradlow morphism Vr,d(C) → Mr,d(C) × Symᵈ(C) for large τ. The space of stability conditions Stab(Vr,d) has a wall at τ = τ_c = 2πd / vol(C), the Bradlow bound. For τ > τ_c, the moduli space is non-empty and the stability conditions are geometric; for τ < τ_c, the moduli space is empty and the stability conditions are non-geometric, corresponding to the empty heart. The wall-crossing formula across τ = τ_c is governed by the Hall algebra of the quiver with potential associated to the vortex moduli space, which is the framed version of the quiver for the moduli space of bundles. The DT invariants of Vr,d(C) are related to the Gromov-Witten invariants of the total space of the determinant line bundle over Mr,d(C) via the vortex/string correspondence. The motivic Hall algebra integration map computes the refined vortex partition function, which satisfies a q-difference equation generalizing the quantum differential equation of the moduli space of bundles. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group, which is isomorphic to ℤr+1 generated by the rank, degree, and vortex number. The autoequivalence group of Dᵇ(Coh(Vr,d)) contains the spherical twists associated to the exceptional collection on the Bradlow limit, and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the q-difference equation.

Worked Example: Wall-Crossing for Vortices on ℙ¹
Consider the moduli space of U(1) vortices of degree d on C = ℙ¹ with τ > 0. The moduli space V1,d(ℙ¹) is isomorphic to ℙ2d+1 for τ > 2πd. Describe the wall-crossing of Bridgeland stability conditions as τ crosses the Bradlow bound τ_c = 2πd, and compute the change in the DT invariant Ω(γ) for the class γ = [𝒪pt].
For U(1) vortices on ℙ¹, the moduli space V1,d(ℙ¹) is the space of degree d effective divisors with a non-vanishing section, which is ℙ2d+1 for τ > τ_c = 2πd. The numerical Grothendieck group is Knum ≅ ℤ² generated by [𝒪] and [𝒪pt]. The central charge is Z(E) = -∫ ch₂(E) + iτ ∫ ch₁(E) + iπ χ(E). For τ > τ_c, the heart is Coh(V) and the DT invariant Ω([𝒪pt]) = 1. As τ → τ_c⁺, the moduli space develops a singularity at the boundary where the section vanishes. The wall-crossing formula in the Hall algebra gives Ωτ<τ_c(γ) = Ωτ>τ_c(γ) + ∑γ₁+γ₂=γ ⟨γ₁, γ₂⟩ Ω(γ₁)Ω(γ₂). For γ = [𝒪pt], the only splitting is γ = [𝒪] + [𝒪pt] - [𝒪] but [𝒪] has Ω = 1. The Euler pairing ⟨[𝒪], [𝒪pt]⟩ = χ(𝒪, 𝒪pt) = 1. Thus Ωτ<τ_c([𝒪pt]) = 1 + 1·1·1 = 2. For τ < τ_c, the moduli space is empty, so the DT invariants are defined via the Hall algebra of the quiver, giving Ω = 2. The jump is ΔΩ = 1, matching the contribution of the boundary divisor in the compactification.
Exam Strategy: Vortex Wall-Crossing
When asked about vortex moduli spaces, always identify the Bradlow bound τ_c = 2πd/vol(C) as the critical wall. The geometric phase τ > τ_c has a smooth moduli space; the non-geometric phase τ < τ_c is described by the quiver Hall algebra. The DT invariant jump is computed by the KS formula using the Euler pairing of the boundary strata. Remember that for U(r) with r > 1, the Bradlow limit is a projective bundle over Mr,d(C), not a symmetric product.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Higgs Bundles with Irregular Singularities and the Wild Character Variety

The moduli space of wild Higgs bundles on a curve C with irregular singularities at marked points p₁, ..., pₙ is a non-compact hyperkähler manifold Mwild(G, C, {p_i}, {Λ_i}) parametrizing pairs (E, φ) where E is a principal G-bundle and φ is a meromorphic Higgs field with prescribed irregular type Λ_i at each p_i. The irregular type is a formal Laurent polynomial Λ_i(z) = ∑k=1m_i Ai,k z-k with coefficients in the Cartan subalgebra, modulo gauge transformations. The wild character variety MBettiwild is the moduli space of meromorphic connections with the same irregular types, related to Mwild by the irregular non-abelian Hodge correspondence of Boalch and Biquard-Boalch. Bridgeland stability conditions on Dᵇ(Coh(Mwild)) are constructed using the irregular Hitchin fibration h: Mwild → Bwild, where the base Bwild is an affine space of dimension ∑_i m_i dim 𝔥 + (g-1) dim G. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫Mwild ch(E) · e-iπ ω · td(Mwild)1/2, with ω a Kähler class pulled back from the wild Hitchin base. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the irregular Hitchin fibration. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mwild) is acted upon by the wild mapping class group, which includes the Stokes data and the formal monodromy. The wall-crossing formula is governed by the Hall algebra of the wild Hitchin system, which is a module over the Hall algebra of the regular Hitchin system. The Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization reproduces the Stokes phenomenon for the irregular connection: the wall-crossing automorphisms are the Stokes matrices. The DT invariants of Mwild are the wild BPS invariants, which satisfy the wild wall-crossing formula of Gaiotto-Moore-Neitzke. The motivic Hall algebra integration map computes the irregular topological string partition function, which is a solution to the quantum differential equation of the wild Hitchin system. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group, which is generated by the classes of the tautological bundles associated to the universal wild Higgs bundle. The autoequivalence group contains the wild spherical twists associated to the vanishing cycles of the irregular Hitchin fibration, and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the irregular isomonodromic deformation equations.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Framed Sheaves and the Donaldson Invariants

The moduli space of framed sheaves on a smooth projective surface S with a divisor D ⊂ S is the space Mr,c₁,c₂fr(S, D) parametrizing pairs (E, φ) where E is a torsion-free sheaf of rank r with Chern classes c₁, c₂, and φ: E|_D → 𝒪_D⊕r is an isomorphism. For S = ℙ² and D = ℙ¹_∞, this is the ADHM moduli space of instantons. For general S, the moduli space is a fine moduli space of dimension 2rc₂ - (r-1)c₁² - r²χ(𝒪_S) + r²D². Bridgeland stability conditions on Dᵇ(Coh(Mr,c₁,c₂fr)) are constructed using the Gieseker-Maruyama stability for framed sheaves. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫M ch(E) · e-iπ ω · td(M)1/2, where ω is a Kähler class coming from the determinant line bundle on the moduli space. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism Mr,c₁,c₂fr → Mr,c₁,c₂ forgetting the framing, which is a projective bundle over the stable locus. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mfr) contains a component isomorphic to the space of stability parameters for the framed quiver, which is ℂr+1 minus a hyperplane arrangement. Wall-crossing corresponds to varying the framing stability parameter, and the KS formula reproduces the blow-up formula for Donaldson invariants. The DT invariants of Mfr are identified with the Donaldson invariants of S via the Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for surfaces: the generating series of DT invariants equals the generating series of Donaldson invariants after a change of variables. The motivic Hall algebra of Mfr is isomorphic to the Hall algebra of the category of framed sheaves, and the integration map to the quantum torus recovers the Nekrasov partition function for the surface S. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group Knum(Mfr) ⊗ ℚ, which is generated by the classes of the tautological bundles associated to the universal framed sheaf. The autoequivalence group contains the spherical twists associated to the exceptional collection on the moduli space of framed sheaves, and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the q-difference equation for the Donaldson invariants.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Perverse Sheaves and the Geometric Satake Correspondence

The moduli space of perverse sheaves on a curve C with singularities at marked points is related to the affine Grassmannian Gr_G = G(ℂ((z)))/G(ℂ[[z]]) via the geometric Satake correspondence. The category of perverse sheaves on Gr_G with convolution product is equivalent to the category of representations of the Langlands dual group G^∨. The moduli space of G-local systems on C with prescribed monodromy at marked points is the character variety M_Betti(G, C). The derived category Dᵇ(Coh(M_Betti(G, C))) carries Bridgeland stability conditions constructed via the non-abelian Hodge correspondence with the moduli space of Higgs bundles M_Higgs(G, C). The central charge is Z(E) = ∫M_Betti ch(E) · e-iπ ω · td(M_Betti)1/2, where ω is the Kähler class from the Hitchin fibration. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Hitchin fibration. The space of stability conditions Stab(M_Betti) is acted upon by the mapping class group of C, which corresponds to the braid group action on Dᵇ(Coh(M_Higgs)) via spherical twists. The wall-crossing formula is the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the Hall algebra of M_Higgs, which matches the monodromy of the Gauss-Manin connection on the cohomology of the Hitchin fibers. The DT invariants of M_Betti are the BPS invariants of the Hitchin system, which are identified with the dimensions of the spaces of conformal blocks via the geometric Langlands correspondence. The motivic Hall algebra integration map computes the topological string partition function of the Hitchin system, which satisfies the quantum differential equation of the Hitchin integrable system. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group, which is isomorphic to the weight lattice of G^∨. The autoequivalence group contains the spherical twists associated to the Hecke eigensheaves, and the braid group action matches the action of the quantum Weyl group on the space of opers. The geometric Satake equivalence lifts to an equivalence of monoidal categories between the spherical Hall algebra of the affine Grassmannian and the Hall algebra of the Hitchin system, intertwining the wall-crossing formulas.
